models.name: CFF (Consistent Force Field)
models.oneLiner: The founding empirical force field: energy as an explicit sum over bonds, angles, torsions, nonbonded pairs
models.description: Lifson and Warshel introduced the idea that a single 'consistent' set of analytic energy functions and parameters could simultaneously reproduce conformations, vibrational spectra, and enthalpies across a whole family of molecules. Crucially, they fit parameters inductively by least-squares against observed data rather than assigning them ad hoc - the conceptual ancestor of every parameter-fitting pipeline that follows, including modern ML reparameterization. Established the canonical functional form (harmonic bonds/angles + periodic torsions + nonbonded terms) still used today. Warshel later shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for multiscale modeling built on this foundation.
models.authors: Shneior Lifson, Arieh Warshel
models.paperTitle: Consistent Force Field for Calculations of Conformations, Vibrational Spectra, and Enthalpies of Cycloalkane and n-Alkane Molecules

models.name: Shepard Interpolation
models.oneLiner: Inverse-distance weighted average of scattered data points; ancestor of all PES interpolation
models.description: Shepard introduced a continuous interpolant for irregularly-spaced data built as a normalised inverse-distance-weighted average of the sampled values. It exactly reproduces the data at the sample points and requires no grid, which is precisely the property needed for potential energy surfaces built from scattered ab initio geometries. Although devised for 2D cartography rather than chemistry, it became the mathematical seed of the modified-Shepard PES program and, more broadly, of the idea that a global surface can be assembled from local information weighted by distance.
models.authors: Donald Shepard
models.paperTitle: A two-dimensional interpolation function for irregularly-spaced data

models.name: MM2 / MM3
models.oneLiner: Allinger's small-molecule force fields; the gold standard for organic geometry and strain energy
models.description: MM2 (1977) refined the CFF idea for organic chemistry using V1/V2 torsional terms and a carefully curated hydrocarbon parameter set, becoming the workhorse for conformational analysis and strain-energy prediction. MM3 (1989) added cross-terms, an improved van der Waals (exp-6) treatment, and was validated against vibrational frequencies, thermodynamics, and crystal data - making it a 'Class II' force field. The MM2/MM3/MM4 series prioritized chemical accuracy on small organics over the speed and biomolecular scale that AMBER/CHARMM chased, and directly seeded MMFF94 and AMOEBA's valence treatment.
models.authors: Norman L. Allinger, Young H. Yuh, Jenn-Huei Lii
models.paperTitle: Conformational analysis. 130. MM2. A hydrocarbon force field utilizing V1 and V2 torsional terms

models.name: CHARMM
models.oneLiner: Biomolecular simulation program + additive all-atom force field for proteins, lipids, nucleic acids
models.description: Brooks et al. released CHARMM as a general program for macromolecular energy minimization and dynamics, paired with an empirical energy function - one of the two pillars (with AMBER) of biomolecular MD. The force field grew through CHARMM22/27 to CHARMM36 and CHARMM36m, with parameters fit to reproduce QM interaction energies and condensed-phase properties. CGenFF (2010) extended it to drug-like molecules via an analogy-based atom typing and penalty score, making CHARMM applicable to arbitrary small molecules. Karplus shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
models.authors: Bernard R. Brooks, Robert E. Bruccoleri, Barry D. Olafson, David J. States, S. Swaminathan, Martin Karplus
models.paperTitle: CHARMM: A program for macromolecular energy, minimization, and dynamics calculations

models.name: EAM
models.oneLiner: Many-body metallic potential: pair terms plus an embedding energy in the local electron density
models.description: Daw and Baskes broke from pure pair potentials for metals by adding an embedding function of the host electron density at each atom, derived from density functional arguments. This many-body term fixed the notorious failures of pair potentials (Cauchy relation, surface relaxation, vacancy formation energies) and made realistic simulation of defects, surfaces, and fracture in metals possible. First appeared as a 1983 PRL on hydrogen embrittlement, with the full derivation in 1984. EAM and its MEAM extension remain the default for metallic MD and are the classical baseline that modern MLIPs for metals are benchmarked against.
models.authors: Murray S. Daw, Michael I. Baskes
models.paperTitle: Embedded-atom method: Derivation and application to impurities, surfaces, and other defects in metals

models.name: Stillinger-Weber
models.oneLiner: Two-body plus explicit three-body angular potential stabilizing tetrahedral silicon
models.description: Stillinger and Weber introduced an explicit three-atom term that penalizes deviation from the tetrahedral angle, letting a simple analytic form stabilize the diamond structure of silicon against denser competitors - something no pair potential could do. This is the canonical 'explicit sum over atom triples' potential and the clearest ancestor of the body-ordered expansion idea that reappears in modern MLIPs (ACE, MACE). Still widely used for silicon, water (mW model), and semiconductor growth simulations decades later.
models.authors: Frank H. Stillinger, Thomas A. Weber
models.paperTitle: Computer simulation of local order in condensed phases of silicon

models.name: Tersoff
models.oneLiner: Bond-order potential: bond strength depends on local coordination environment
models.description: Tersoff made the pair-bond strength an explicit function of the local environment (coordination number and bond angles) via a bond-order factor, following Abell's chemical pseudopotential arguments. This let one parameter set describe multiple coordination states of silicon and carbon - bonds form and break naturally as the environment changes. The bond-order concept is the direct ancestor of REBO, AIREBO, and ReaxFF, and is the classical precursor of environment-dependent ML descriptors. Note the 1988 PRB 37, 6991 paper is the refined form; an earlier 1986 PRL introduced the approach.
models.authors: Jerry Tersoff
institutions: IBM T. J. Watson Research Center
models.paperTitle: New empirical approach for the structure and energy of covalent systems

models.name: REBO / AIREBO
models.fullName: Reactive Empirical Bond Order / Adaptive Intermolecular REBO
models.oneLiner: Reactive hydrocarbon bond-order potentials; AIREBO adds dispersion and torsion
models.description: Brenner adapted Tersoff's bond-order form to hydrocarbons for simulating diamond CVD, adding correction terms so that radicals, conjugation, and bond breaking were described correctly - the first widely used reactive potential for organic chemistry. The 2002 second-generation REBO (Brenner et al., J. Phys. Condens. Matter 14, 783) improved the analytic forms and database. AIREBO (Stuart et al., 2000) grafted on adaptive Lennard-Jones dispersion and explicit torsional terms so that intermolecular packing - critical for polymers, nanotubes, and tribology - was captured alongside reactivity.
models.authors: Donald W. Brenner; Steven J. Stuart, Alan B. Tutein, Judith A. Harrison
models.paperTitle: Empirical potential for hydrocarbons for use in simulating the chemical vapor deposition of diamond films
models.venue: Phys. Rev. B 42, 9458 (1990); AIREBO: J. Chem. Phys. 112, 6472 (2000)

models.name: Modified Shepard Interpolation
models.fullName: Modified Shepard interpolation of molecular potential energy surfaces (Collins)
models.oneLiner: PES from Shepard-weighted local Taylor expansions at ab initio data points
models.description: Ischtwan and Collins replaced Shepard's constant data values with second-order Taylor expansions of the energy built from the ab initio energy, gradient and Hessian at each reference configuration, then Shepard-weighted them into a global surface. Because each datum carries curvature information, the interpolant converges to the exact PES with far fewer expensive electronic-structure calls, and the weights are symmetrised over permutations of like atoms. The scheme pioneered the 'grow the PES where the dynamics goes' strategy: configurations are added iteratively from classical trajectories, an early ancestor of modern active learning.
models.authors: Josef Ischtwan, Michael A. Collins
models.paperTitle: Molecular potential energy surfaces by interpolation

models.name: AMBER (ff94)
models.fullName: Assisted Model Building with Energy Refinement - second generation force field
models.oneLiner: Second-generation biomolecular force field with RESP charges; the template for drug-discovery MD
models.description: Cornell, Kollman and coworkers defined the second-generation AMBER functional form - a deliberately simple Class I model (harmonic bonds/angles, cosine torsions, 12-6 LJ, fixed point charges) - and paired it with RESP charges fit to HF/6-31G* electrostatic potentials. The simplicity was the point: it made large-scale protein and nucleic acid MD tractable and reproducible. The ff94 lineage (ff99SB, ff14SB, ff19SB) remains the most-used protein force field family, and 'Amber-compatible' is still the compatibility target that GAFF, OpenFF, Espaloma, and ByteFF all aim at.
models.authors: Wendy D. Cornell, Piotr Cieplak, Christopher I. Bayly, Ian R. Gould, Kenneth M. Merz, David M. Ferguson, David C. Spellmeyer, Thomas Fox, James W. Caldwell, Peter A. Kollman
models.paperTitle: A Second Generation Force Field for the Simulation of Proteins, Nucleic Acids, and Organic Molecules

models.name: MMFF94
models.oneLiner: Broad-coverage organic force field fit largely to high-quality MP2 quantum data
models.description: Halgren's MMFF94 was published as a five-part series covering the functional form, van der Waals/electrostatics, geometries and vibrational frequencies, conformational energies, and empirical extension rules. Its distinguishing feature was near-complete coverage of drug-like organic chemistry with parameters derived primarily from a large, deliberately constructed MP2/6-31G* dataset supplemented by experiment - an early large-scale QM-to-FF fitting effort in the spirit of what Espaloma and ByteFF later automated with GNNs. It borrows MM3's Class II flavor while remaining broadly transferable, and is still the default in many cheminformatics toolkits (RDKit, Open Babel) for conformer generation.
models.authors: Thomas A. Halgren
models.paperTitle: Merck molecular force field. I. Basis, form, scope, parameterization, and performance of MMFF94

models.name: OPLS-AA
models.fullName: Optimized Potentials for Liquid Simulations - All Atom
models.oneLiner: All-atom force field parameterized against experimental organic liquid properties
models.description: Jorgensen's distinguishing choice was to fit nonbonded parameters directly to experimental condensed-phase data - densities and heats of vaporization of pure organic liquids - rather than to gas-phase QM. OPLS-AA extended the earlier united-atom OPLS to all atoms, borrowing bonded parameters from AMBER but rederiving torsions and nonbonded terms. This 'fit to the property you care about' philosophy made OPLS strong for solvation and partition coefficients, and it prefigures the modern practice of training MLIPs on condensed-phase observables.
models.authors: William L. Jorgensen, David S. Maxwell, Julian Tirado-Rives
models.paperTitle: Development and Testing of the OPLS All-Atom Force Field on Conformational Energetics and Properties of Organic Liquids

models.name: Product PES / POTFIT
models.fullName: Product representation of potential energy surfaces
models.oneLiner: PES as a sum of products of 1D functions, enabling MCTDH quantum dynamics
models.description: Jäckle and Meyer showed how to refit a multidimensional PES as a linear combination of products of one-dimensional natural potentials, determined by an iterative Tucker-like decomposition of the potential tensor on a product grid. The sum-of-products form is what makes the multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (MCTDH) method tractable, since the multidimensional integrals factorise. It established the tensor-decomposition lineage of PES representation (later multigrid POTFIT, multilayer POTFIT) that runs parallel to the polynomial-fitting lineage.
models.authors: Andreas Jäckle, Hans-Dieter Meyer
models.paperTitle: Product representation of potential energy surfaces

models.name: n-Mode Representation
models.fullName: n-mode (hierarchical many-mode) representation of the potential
models.oneLiner: Hierarchical expansion of the PES in 1-mode, 2-mode, 3-mode... coupling terms
models.description: Carter, Culik and Bowman introduced a hierarchical decomposition of the full potential in normal coordinates into a sum of one-mode, two-mode, three-mode (and higher) coupling contributions, truncated at low n. The representation tames the exponential scaling of grid-based PES construction and is the backbone of practical VSCF/VCI vibrational spectroscopy for polyatomics. Conceptually it is the intramolecular sibling of the many-body expansion that later underpinned MB-pol and q-AQUA: both buy accuracy by truncating a rapidly converging hierarchy of couplings rather than fitting the full-dimensional function at once.
models.authors: Stuart Carter, Susan J. Culik, Joel M. Bowman
models.paperTitle: Vibrational self-consistent field method for many-mode systems: A new approach and application to the vibrations of CO adsorbed on Cu(100)

models.name: COMPASS
models.fullName: Condensed-phase Optimized Molecular Potentials for Atomistic Simulation Studies
models.oneLiner: Class II ab initio force field with cross-terms, validated on condensed-phase properties
models.description: Sun combined the two dominant parameterization philosophies: derive valence parameters and cross-terms from ab initio data, then refine nonbonded parameters against experimental condensed-phase densities and cohesive energies via MD. The result was a Class II force field (anharmonic bonds, extensive cross-terms) covering organics, polymers, and some inorganics in one consistent scheme. Widely adopted for polymer and materials simulation and commercialized in Accelrys/BIOVIA Materials Studio.
models.authors: Huai Sun
models.paperTitle: COMPASS: An ab Initio Force-Field Optimized for Condensed-Phase Applications - Overview with Details on Alkane and Benzene Compounds

models.name: ReaxFF
models.oneLiner: General reactive force field with bond-order-dependent terms and dynamic charge equilibration
models.description: van Duin and Goddard generalized bond-order potentials into a broadly transferable reactive framework: all valence terms decay smoothly with bond order, and charges are recomputed on the fly by electronegativity equalization (QEq), so bonds break, form, and charges redistribute during a simulation. Parameters came from QM bond dissociation curves and reaction energies plus heats of formation. Reported accuracy comparable to or better than PM3 at roughly 100x the speed, enabling million-atom simulations of combustion, catalysis, and explosives. ReaxFF was for two decades the main way to do reactive MD at scale, and is the classical benchmark that reactive MLIPs must beat.
models.authors: Adri C. T. van Duin, Siddharth Dasgupta, Francois Lorant, William A. Goddard III
models.paperTitle: ReaxFF: A Reactive Force Field for Hydrocarbons

models.name: Drude oscillator FF
models.fullName: Classical Drude oscillator polarizable force field
models.oneLiner: Polarization via charged auxiliary particles on springs, integrated by extended Lagrangian MD
models.description: Lamoureux and Roux formalized the classical Drude (charge-on-spring) approach for MD: each polarizable atom carries an auxiliary charged particle harmonically tethered to it, whose displacement represents induced dipole response. Their key contribution was an extended-Lagrangian integration scheme with a cold Drude thermostat, making polarizable MD only modestly more expensive than additive MD rather than requiring self-consistent iteration. This became the basis of the CHARMM Drude-2013 polarizable force field for proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids - the main alternative to AMOEBA's induced-dipole route.
models.authors: Guillaume Lamoureux, Benoît Roux
models.paperTitle: Modeling induced polarization with classical Drude oscillators: Theory and molecular dynamics simulation algorithm

models.name: GAFF / GAFF2
models.oneLiner: Amber-compatible general small-molecule force field with rule-based atom typing
models.description: GAFF extended AMBER beyond proteins and nucleic acids to essentially any drug-like organic molecule (H, C, N, O, S, P, halogens) using a broad set of atom types plus empirical and heuristic rules to estimate missing force constants. Combined with AM1-BCC charges it enabled fully automated small-molecule parameterization - the workflow behind most protein-ligand free energy calculations for two decades. Its weakness, the rule-based discrete atom-typing bottleneck, is precisely what OpenFF's SMIRNOFF typing and later Espaloma's GNN typing were built to replace. GAFF2 is an ongoing refit with improved torsions and vdW parameters (widely distributed in AmberTools, though never given a standalone canonical paper).
models.authors: Junmei Wang, Romain M. Wolf, James W. Caldwell, Peter A. Kollman, David A. Case
models.paperTitle: Development and testing of a general amber force field

keyMetrics.value: H, C, N, O, S, P, halogens

models.name: GROMOS
models.oneLiner: United-atom biomolecular force field parameterized against free energies of hydration and solvation
models.description: GROMOS traces to van Gunsteren's Groningen work in the 1980s, but the 53A5/53A6 paper is the canonical modern reference: its defining choice was to fit partial charges to reproduce experimental free enthalpies of hydration in water and solvation in cyclohexane, rather than QM electrostatic potentials. This thermodynamic-target philosophy contrasts sharply with AMBER's RESP approach and makes GROMOS strong for partitioning and membrane work. It retains a united-atom treatment (aliphatic hydrogens absorbed into carbons) for speed. Later refined as 54A7 (2011).
models.authors: Chris Oostenbrink, Alessandra Villa, Alan E. Mark, Wilfred F. van Gunsteren
models.paperTitle: A biomolecular force field based on the free enthalpy of hydration and solvation: The GROMOS force-field parameter sets 53A5 and 53A6

models.name: Behler-Parrinello HDNNP (2G-HDNNP)
models.oneLiner: The founding atomic-decomposition NNP: total energy = sum of element-wise atomic NN energies
models.description: Introduced the decomposition of the total energy into a sum of atomic contributions, each predicted by a small element-specific feed-forward network taking a symmetry-function fingerprint of that atom's local environment within a cutoff. This single idea — extensivity plus permutation/rotation/translation invariance by construction — made NNPs applicable to systems of arbitrary size and is the ancestor of essentially every modern MLIP. Demonstrated on bulk silicon at orders-of-magnitude lower cost than DFT. The reference implementation is the Fortran code RuNNer (https://gitlab.com/TheochemGoettingen/RuNNer, docs https://theochemgoettingen.gitlab.io/RuNNer/1.3/), still developed in the Behler group at Göttingen; n2p2 (https://github.com/CompPhysVienna/n2p2) is the widely used LAMMPS-coupled reimplementation.
models.authors: Jörg Behler, Michele Parrinello
models.paperTitle: Generalized Neural-Network Representation of High-Dimensional Potential-Energy Surfaces

models.name: CCpol
models.oneLiner: First-principles CCSD(T) water dimer potential that predicted bulk water properties
models.description: Bukowski, Szalewicz, Groenenboom and van der Avoird fitted a water pair potential to coupled-cluster and SAPT dimer interaction energies and combined it with a three-body term and polarisation, then predicted second virial coefficients, dimer VRT spectra and liquid-water structure without empirical adjustment. It was the landmark demonstration that bulk water properties could be reached from first principles alone, and the site-site refit CCpol-8s made the surface cheap enough for condensed-phase simulation. CCpol set the accuracy target and the many-body/polarisation architecture that MB-pol and q-AQUA later inherited and surpassed.
models.authors: Robert Bukowski, Krzysztof Szalewicz, Gerrit C. Groenenboom, Ad van der Avoird
models.paperTitle: Predictions of the properties of water from first principles

models.name: GAP
models.oneLiner: First Gaussian-process interatomic potential: QM accuracy without the electrons
models.description: Introduced Gaussian process (kernel) regression as a way to fit the potential energy surface directly from DFT energies and forces, with no fixed functional form. GAP established the non-parametric, data-driven paradigm for interatomic potentials and the practice of learning from forces as well as energies. Originally used bispectrum descriptors of the neighbour density; later canonically paired with SOAP. Its built-in Bayesian error estimate seeded the whole active-learning subfield.
models.authors: Albert P. Bartók, Mike C. Payne, Risi Kondor, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: Gaussian Approximation Potentials: The Accuracy of Quantum Mechanics, without the Electrons

models.name: PIP
models.oneLiner: Global linear fit of PES in symmetrised polynomials of Morse variables of all interatomic distances
models.description: Braams and Bowman established the canonical recipe for global PES fitting: expand the energy in polynomials of Morse-transformed internuclear distances that are symmetrised over the permutation group of identical atoms, then solve a single linear least-squares problem against tens of thousands of scattered ab initio energies. Invariance to translation, rotation and like-atom permutation is exact by construction rather than learned, and the fit is linear so it is fast, stable and reproducible. First applied to CH5+ around 2003 (invariant under all 120 permutations of five hydrogens), the method became the standard for spectroscopically accurate small-molecule and reactive surfaces; this 2009 review is its canonical statement.
models.authors: Bastiaan J. Braams, Joel M. Bowman
models.paperTitle: Permutationally invariant potential energy surfaces in high dimensionality

keyMetrics.value: tens of cm^-1 over tens of thousands of ab initio energies

models.name: AMOEBA
models.fullName: Atomic Multipole Optimized Energetics for Biomolecular Applications
models.oneLiner: Polarizable multipole force field: permanent atomic multipoles plus self-consistent induced dipoles
models.description: AMOEBA replaces fixed point charges with permanent atomic multipoles through quadrupole, and adds mutual polarization via self-consistently converged induced dipoles with Thole damping. This gives a genuinely physical description of electrostatics in heterogeneous environments - ions, metal centers, and binding pockets - where additive force fields systematically fail. The cost is roughly an order of magnitude over additive FFs, which motivated GPU implementations (OpenMM, Tinker-HP). AMOEBA is the reference polarizable model that modern GNN-parameterized polarizable force fields such as ByteFF-Pol are measured against.
models.authors: Jay W. Ponder, Chuanjie Wu, Pengyu Ren, Vijay S. Pande, John D. Chodera, Michael J. Schnieders, Imran Haque, David L. Mobley, Daniel S. Lambrecht, Robert A. DiStasio Jr., Martin Head-Gordon, Gary N. I. Clark, Margaret E. Johnson, Teresa Head-Gordon
models.paperTitle: Current Status of the AMOEBA Polarizable Force Field

models.name: MSA
models.oneLiner: Practical recursive generator of PIP bases for arbitrary symmetry and polynomial order
models.description: Xie and Bowman turned PIP fitting from a bespoke art into usable software by symmetrising a primitive monomial basis and evaluating each invariant polynomial recursively from sums of products of previously computed monomials. This made bases for many permutational symmetry groups and high polynomial orders generatable automatically and cheap to evaluate, and it was validated on a new H3O+ surface fitted to roughly 62,000 ab initio energies. The resulting MSA code (later MSA-2.0) is the workhorse behind most published PIP surfaces, including the water many-body fits.
models.authors: Zhen Xie, Joel M. Bowman
models.paperTitle: Permutationally Invariant Polynomial Basis for Molecular Energy Surface Fitting via Monomial Symmetrization

models.name: 3G-HDNNP
models.oneLiner: HDNNP plus a second NN predicting environment-dependent atomic charges for long-range electrostatics
models.description: Extends the 2G scheme with a parallel set of atomic neural networks that predict local partial charges from the same ACSF fingerprints; these charges give an explicit Ewald/Coulomb electrostatic energy beyond the short-range cutoff, which is subtracted from the reference energies before training the short-range NNs. First applied to multicomponent ZnO. This fixed 2G's blindness to long-range electrostatics but retained a fundamental limitation: charges are still purely local functions of the environment, so genuinely non-local charge transfer and multiple charge states cannot be captured — precisely the gap that CENT and 4G-HDNNP later closed.
models.authors: Nongnuch Artrith, Tobias Morawietz, Jörg Behler
models.paperTitle: High-dimensional neural-network potentials for multicomponent systems: Applications to zinc oxide

models.name: ACSF
models.oneLiner: Radial (G2) and angular (G4/G5) symmetry functions — the canonical hand-crafted atomic fingerprint
models.description: The definitive methods paper for the descriptor half of the Behler-Parrinello scheme. It systematically defines and analyzes radial and angular symmetry function families (G1-G5) built from cutoff-damped two- and three-body terms, giving a fixed-length, invariant, differentiable fingerprint of an atom's environment. ACSFs became the default input layer for HDNNPs, ANI, and many descriptor-NN codes, and remain the reference against which SOAP, ACE, MTP and learned descriptors are compared. Their main weakness — the number of symmetry functions scales combinatorially with the number of elements — motivated later variants such as wACSF (weighted ACSF, Gastegger et al., arXiv:1712.05861, J. Chem. Phys. 148, 241709 (2018), doi:10.1063/1.5019667), which replaces element-resolved function sets with element-weighted ones and keeps the descriptor size constant across chemical space.
models.authors: Jörg Behler
models.paperTitle: Atom-centered symmetry functions for constructing high-dimensional neural network potentials

models.name: Coulomb Matrix + KRR
models.fullName: Coulomb Matrix with Kernel Ridge Regression
models.oneLiner: First ML model to predict molecular atomization energies from nuclear charges and coordinates alone
models.description: Recast solving the molecular Schrodinger equation as a nonlinear regression problem, representing a molecule by a matrix of pairwise nuclear repulsion terms (the Coulomb matrix) and regressing atomization energies with kernel ridge regression. Trained on ~7k small organic molecules from GDB, it reached ~10 kcal/mol MAE — crude by modern standards, but it established the entire supervised-learning-on-chemical-space paradigm. Introduced the QM7 dataset and the descriptor+kernel template that dominated the field until 2017. Its permutation ambiguity (row ordering) motivated nearly every representation that followed.
models.authors: Matthias Rupp, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Klaus-Robert Müller, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
institutions: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
models.paperTitle: Fast and Accurate Modeling of Molecular Atomization Energies with Machine Learning

keyMetrics.benchmark: QM9 (as benchmarked in Gilmer et al. 2017)

models.name: SOAP
models.oneLiner: Rotationally invariant atomic-density overlap kernel; the canonical density-trick descriptor
models.description: Defines a smooth Gaussian atomic neighbour density and constructs a similarity measure by integrating the overlap of two densities over all rotations, yielding a smooth, invariant, and highly faithful representation. The paper's deeper contribution is showing that many prior descriptors are special cases of one general density-expansion approach using increasing angular wave numbers. The power spectrum of the spherical-harmonic expansion coefficients is the object nearly every later density-SH method generalizes. Preprint appeared 2012; published PRB 2013.
models.authors: Albert P. Bartók, Risi Kondor, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: On representing chemical environments

models.name: MB-pol
models.oneLiner: First-principles water potential: PIP 2-body and 3-body terms plus classical polarisation
models.description: Babin, Leforestier and Paesani built a water model directly on the many-body expansion: an explicit CCSD(T)-quality two-body term and a three-body term, each fitted with permutationally invariant polynomials over flexible monomers, with all higher-body physics carried by classical many-body polarisation. Developed across three papers (dimer/VRT spectrum and second virial 2013, trimer and third virial 2014, liquid phase 2014), it reproduces water from the dimer through clusters to liquid and ice without empirical fitting to bulk data. MB-pol became the reference 'first-principles' water potential and the template for data-driven many-body PEFs generally.
models.authors: Volodymyr Babin, Claude Leforestier, Gregory R. Medders, Francesco Paesani
models.paperTitle: Development of a "First Principles" Water Potential with Flexible Monomers: Dimer Potential Energy Surface, VRT Spectrum, and Second Virial Coefficient

keyMetrics.value: single potential across all phases without bulk fitting

models.name: PIP-NN
models.oneLiner: Feed low-order PIPs into a neural network to get symmetry-exact nonlinear PES fits
models.description: Jiang and Guo solved the long-standing problem that plain neural-network PES fits break permutation symmetry, by using low-order permutationally invariant polynomials as the input layer of the network. Symmetry is then exact by construction while the network supplies nonlinear flexibility that a purely linear PIP expansion lacks, so fewer polynomial terms are needed for the same accuracy. Demonstrated on H + H2 and Cl + H2 with quantum-scattering-grade fidelity, PIP-NN became the dominant approach for reactive scattering surfaces and spawned a long series (four-atom systems, diabatic matrices, Delta-ML variants, GPU codes).
models.authors: Bin Jiang, Hua Guo
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
models.paperTitle: Permutation invariant polynomial neural network approach to fitting potential energy surfaces

keyMetrics.value: reproduces analytic PES to quantum-scattering accuracy

models.name: SNAP
models.oneLiner: Linear fit of atomic energy to bispectrum components on 4D hyperspherical harmonics
models.description: Characterizes each atom's neighbour density by projecting it onto a basis of hyperspherical harmonics in four dimensions and taking bispectrum components, then assumes a purely linear relation between atom energy and those components. The linearity makes fitting a simple least-squares problem and makes evaluation fast and robust enough for large-scale MD. Its tight LAMMPS integration made the density-trick approach practical for production materials simulation at Sandia scale. Preprint 2014; published JCP 2015.
models.authors: Aidan P. Thompson, Laura P. Swiler, Christian R. Trott, Stephen M. Foiles, Garritt J. Tucker
models.paperTitle: Spectral neighbor analysis method for automated generation of quantum-accurate interatomic potentials

models.name: BoB
models.oneLiner: Bags Coulomb-matrix elements by atom-pair type, fixing the CM's permutation problem
models.description: Reorganizes the Coulomb matrix's off-diagonal elements into 'bags' grouped by element pair (C-C, C-H, ...), each bag sorted by magnitude — yielding a permutation-invariant, fixed-length vector inspired by bag-of-words. This simple change cut atomization-energy errors several-fold over the raw Coulomb matrix and made the descriptor+KRR approach genuinely competitive. The paper also analyzed nonlocality in chemical space and the many-body character of the learned potential. BoB remained a standard baseline for years.
models.authors: Katja Hansen, Franziska Biegler, Raghunathan Ramakrishnan, Wiktor Pronobis, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld, Klaus-Robert Müller, Alexandre Tkatchenko
institutions: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
models.paperTitle: Machine Learning Predictions of Molecular Properties: Accurate Many-Body Potentials and Nonlocality in Chemical Space

keyMetrics.benchmark: QM9 (as benchmarked in Gilmer et al. 2017)

keyMetrics.value: 0.80x chemical accuracy — best of the hand-crafted descriptors

models.name: CENT
models.fullName: Charge Equilibration via Neural network Technique
models.oneLiner: Neural nets predict environment-dependent electronegativities; charges come from global charge equilibration
models.description: Inverts the usual NNP logic: instead of a network emitting an atomic energy directly, atomic networks emit environment-dependent electronegativities that feed a classical QEq-style charge-equilibration functional, whose minimization over the whole system yields the atomic charges and the total energy. Because equilibration is global, CENT captures non-local charge redistribution that any purely local descriptor-sum model misses, and it is especially well suited to ionic systems. Directly seeded the fourth-generation HDNNP line (Ko, Finkler, Goedecker, Behler) and modern charge-equilibration MLIPs; refined as CENT2 (Phys. Rev. B 105, 144106 (2022), https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.144106).
models.authors: S. Alireza Ghasemi, Albert Hofstetter, Santanu Saha, Stefan Goedecker
institutions: Institute for Advanced Studies in Basic Sciences (IASBS), Zanjan
models.paperTitle: Interatomic potentials for ionic systems with density functional accuracy based on charge densities obtained by a neural network

models.name: Delta-ML
models.oneLiner: Learn the correction from a cheap QM baseline to a high-level target instead of the property itself
models.description: Rather than learning a property from scratch, Δ-ML learns the difference between a cheap electronic-structure method (e.g. PM7, HF) and an expensive target (e.g. DFT, CCSD(T)). Because the residual is smoother and smaller than the raw property, the model needs far less training data to reach chemical accuracy, and it inherits the baseline's physics for free. Demonstrated on enthalpies, free energies, entropies and electron-correlation energies, and shown transferable when trained on 1-10% of a large organic dataset. The Δ-learning trick is now ubiquitous, underpinning OrbNet, Δ-DFT corrections, and most transfer-learning-to-coupled-cluster work.
models.authors: Raghunathan Ramakrishnan, Pavlo O. Dral, Matthias Rupp, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
institutions: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
models.paperTitle: Big Data Meets Quantum Chemistry Approximations: The Δ-Machine Learning Approach

keyMetrics.value: Chemical accuracy reached from a cheap baseline with a fraction of the training data
Correlation energies predicted at Hartree-Fock cost

models.name: MTP
models.oneLiner: Linear basis of contracted Cartesian moment tensors; the founding density-trick Cartesian potential.
models.description: Shapeev introduced moment tensor potentials, which describe each atomic neighborhood by 'moments' — radial functions weighted by outer products of interatomic direction vectors, giving Cartesian tensors of arbitrary rank. Rotationally invariant basis functions are formed by fully contracting these tensors with each other, and the energy is linear in that basis, so fitting is a linear least-squares problem. This is the Cartesian analogue of the spherical-harmonic 'density trick' used by SOAP/ACE, and it established systematic improvability (completeness in body order and polynomial degree) as a design principle. MTP remains one of the most cost-effective MLIPs for metals, alloys and defects.
models.authors: Alexander V. Shapeev
institutions: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology
models.paperTitle: Moment Tensor Potentials: a class of systematically improvable interatomic potentials

models.name: BAML
models.oneLiner: Many-body expansion descriptor injecting force-field-like bonded terms into the ML representation
models.description: Built a hierarchy of representations meeting explicit uniqueness and target-similarity criteria, using a many-body expansion that encodes bonded, angular and higher-order terms with classical force-field functional forms (Morse, harmonic angle, torsion) rather than bare Coulomb terms. The insight was that a representation should resemble the actual potential energy surface it must regress — 'target similarity'. BAML improved on BoB across atomization energies, vibrational energies, dipole moments and electronic properties, and this analysis of uniqueness/similarity influenced the design of FCHL and later descriptors.
models.authors: Bing Huang, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
models.paperTitle: Communication: Understanding molecular representations in machine learning: The role of uniqueness and target similarity

keyMetrics.benchmark: QM9 (as benchmarked in Gilmer et al. 2017)

models.name: DTNN
models.oneLiner: First message-passing net on molecules, with tensor-factorized interactions and local chemical potentials
models.description: Schütt et al. unified many-body Hamiltonian concepts with a deep network in which atom embeddings are refined by pairwise interaction passes modulated through a factorized tensor layer on interatomic distances. Energies are a size-extensive sum of atomic contributions, giving uniform ~1 kcal/mol accuracy across compositional and configurational space. Crucially it produced spatially and chemically resolved insight — local chemical potential maps that, for instance, classified aromatic rings by stability. It is the direct ancestor of SchNet and the first true molecular MPNN.
models.authors: Kristof T. Schütt, Farhad Arbabzadah, Stefan Chmiela, Klaus-Robert Müller, Alexandre Tkatchenko
models.paperTitle: Quantum-chemical insights from deep tensor neural networks

models.name: MB-nrg
models.oneLiner: MB-pol's architecture generalised to ions, gases and mixtures from CCSD(T)-F12 data
models.description: Bajaj, Götz and Paesani extended the MB-pol formalism beyond neat water: explicit one-, two- and three-body terms fitted with PIPs to CCSD(T)-F12 reference data, with higher orders from classical induction, first for halide–water and then alkali-metal–water dimers. The family (with its classical counterpart TTM-nrg) now covers ion hydration, CO2/H2O mixtures and other molecular fluids, all compatible with MB-pol so heterogeneous systems can be assembled from matched components. The associated MB-Fit toolchain automates the PIP fitting workflow, and active-learning variants have been used to sample many-body configuration space efficiently.
models.authors: Pushp Bajaj, Andreas W. Götz, Marc Riera, Narbe Mardirossian, Francesco Paesani
models.paperTitle: Toward Chemical Accuracy in the Description of Ion–Water Interactions through Many-Body Representations. I. Halide–Water Dimer Potential Energy Surfaces

keyMetrics.value: CCSD(T)-F12 at the complete basis set limit

models.name: ANI-1
models.fullName: ANAKIN-ME (Accurate NeurAl networK engINe for Molecular Energies)
models.oneLiner: Transferable HDNNP for organic molecules using modified ACSFs (AEVs) trained on ~20M DFT conformers
models.description: Took the Behler-Parrinello architecture out of single-system fitting and made it a general-purpose organic-chemistry potential. Key changes: modified ACSFs ("atomic environment vectors", AEVs) with species-resolved angular terms, and massive-scale training on the ANI-1 dataset (~20M off-equilibrium conformations of ~57k small molecules, CHNO only, at ωB97X/6-31G*). Achieved DFT-quality energies at force-field cost and demonstrated transferability to molecules much larger than those trained on — the template for every subsequent pretrained molecular NNP.
models.authors: Justin S. Smith, Olexandr Isayev, Adrian E. Roitberg
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
models.paperTitle: ANI-1: an extensible neural network potential with DFT accuracy at force field computational cost

models.name: CGCNN
models.oneLiner: First general crystal-graph GNN: periodic multigraphs for interpretable materials property prediction
models.description: Xie and Grossman brought graph convolutions to periodic solids by representing a crystal as an undirected weighted multigraph — atoms in one unit cell as nodes, multiple edges to periodic images within a cutoff, each edge featurized by distance. A pooling step over atoms gives per-crystal properties, and per-site energy contributions can be extracted, giving chemical interpretability (they used it to mine design rules for perovskites). CGCNN is the founding architecture of materials-informatics GNNs and the ancestor of MEGNet, ALIGNN and M3GNet.
models.authors: Tian Xie, Jeffrey C. Grossman
models.paperTitle: Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for an Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Material Properties

models.name: FCHL18 / FCHL19
models.oneLiner: Alchemical + structural distribution descriptor; the high-water mark of kernel QML accuracy
models.description: FCHL18 represents each atom by scaled 2- and 3-body distribution functions over both structural and *alchemical* (element-identity) degrees of freedom, placing elements in a continuous space defined by periodic-table coordinates. This enables alchemical extrapolation — predicting bonds between element pairs absent from training. It set the accuracy record for kernel models on QM9 and remains the strongest low-data method. FCHL19 re-engineered the representation as a discretized, fixed-size vector, trading a little accuracy for orders-of-magnitude speedup, making kernel QML practical on large sets.
models.authors: Felix A. Faber, Anders S. Christensen, Bing Huang, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld (FCHL18); Anders S. Christensen, Lars A. Bratholm, Felix A. Faber, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld (FCHL19)
models.paperTitle: Alchemical and structural distribution based representation for universal quantum machine learning (FCHL18); FCHL revisited: faster and more accurate quantum machine learning (FCHL19)
models.venue: J. Chem. Phys. 2018 (FCHL18); J. Chem. Phys. 2020 (FCHL19)

models.name: GDML
models.oneLiner: Kernel model learned in the force (gradient) domain, so energy conservation is exact
models.description: Chmiela, Tkatchenko, Müller and co-workers reframed force-field learning: instead of fitting energies and differentiating, they fit forces directly with a kernel whose covariance is the Hessian of an energy kernel, so the learned forces are an exact gradient field and energy conservation holds by construction. Training on forces also exploits 3N labels per configuration instead of one, which is why ~1000 conformations from an AIMD trajectory suffice. It reached ~0.3 kcal/mol on energies and ~1 kcal/mol/Å on forces for mid-sized molecules and, crucially, kept a global molecular descriptor rather than assuming locality — the defining contrast with the atom-centred branch.
models.authors: Stefan Chmiela, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Huziel E. Sauceda, Igor Poltavsky, Kristof T. Schütt, Klaus-Robert Müller
models.paperTitle: Machine learning of accurate energy-conserving molecular force fields

models.name: HDAD
models.fullName: Histograms of Distances, Angles and Dihedrals
models.oneLiner: Simple internal-coordinate histograms that beat every other hand-crafted descriptor on QM9 energetics
models.description: Part of the landmark Faber et al. benchmark that compared many representations (CM, BoB, BAML, ECFP4, HD/HDA/HDAD, MARAD) crossed with several regressors (KRR, random forest, neural nets, graph convolutions) on QM9 under an identical split. HDAD simply histograms interatomic distances, angles and dihedrals — and this unglamorous choice won on energetic targets, delivering the first ML predictions with errors below hybrid-DFT's own error versus experiment. The paper set the evaluation protocol and the 13-target QM9 leaderboard that Gilmer and everyone after adopted.
models.authors: Felix A. Faber, Luke Hutchison, Bing Huang, Justin Gilmer, Samuel S. Schoenholz, George E. Dahl, Oriol Vinyals, Steven Kearnes, Patrick F. Riley, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
models.paperTitle: Prediction Errors of Molecular Machine Learning Models Lower than Hybrid DFT Error

models.name: MBTR
models.oneLiner: Unified stratified many-body descriptor covering both finite molecules and periodic crystals
models.description: Generalizes the CM/BoB/HDAD family into a single smooth, stratified tensor: k-body terms (atom counts, inverse distances, angles) are broadcast into Gaussian-smeared distributions indexed by element combination. Critically, it applies unchanged to both molecules and periodic solids, which earlier molecular descriptors could not do — a step toward a shared representation across chemistry and materials science. Widely used through the DScribe package and a standard baseline for descriptor-based kernel models.
models.authors: Haoyan Huo, Matthias Rupp
institutions: Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society
models.paperTitle: Unified representation of molecules and crystals for machine learning

keyMetrics.value: Single descriptor family valid for both molecules and periodic crystals

models.name: MPNN
models.oneLiner: Unifying framework that recast existing molecular GNNs as message passing, readout, and update
models.description: Gilmer et al. showed that a large family of existing graph models for chemistry (molecular fingerprints, GGNN, interaction networks, DTNN, laplacian-based convnets) are special cases of a single abstraction: message functions, vertex update functions, and a readout. They then searched within that design space, introducing edge networks and a set2set readout, and reached chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 QM9 targets. The paper is the organizing vocabulary of the whole field — nearly every later architecture describes itself in MPNN terms.
models.authors: Justin Gilmer, Samuel S. Schoenholz, Patrick F. Riley, Oriol Vinyals, George E. Dahl
models.paperTitle: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

models.name: SLATM / aSLATM + amons
models.fullName: Spectrum of London and Axilrod-Teller-Muto potential; atoms-in-molecules fragments
models.description: Introduced two ideas in one paper. SLATM builds a descriptor from the spectrum of physically-motivated London dispersion and Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body potentials; aSLATM is its atomic (local) decomposition. 'Amons' are small atom-in-molecule fragments selected on the fly by active learning, so a model trained only on tiny fragments reconstructs the chemistry of much larger query systems. Together they gave transferable QML that scales to DNA base pairs and proteins from training on small molecules, and reframed chemical space as compositional — 'an extension of the periodic table that accounts for chemical environments'.
models.oneLiner: Physics-based spectral descriptor plus on-the-fly molecular fragments for transferable QML
models.authors: Bing Huang, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
models.paperTitle: Quantum machine learning using atom-in-molecule-based fragments selected on the fly

keyMetrics.value: Reaches chemical accuracy; competitive with FCHL18 in kernel-model comparisons
Energies, forces, charges, NMR shifts, polarizabilities from small-fragment training up to DNA base pairs and proteins

models.name: SchNet
models.oneLiner: Continuous-filter convolutions on atom positions; the canonical invariant molecular GNN
models.description: SchNet replaced discrete grid convolutions with continuous-filter convolutional layers whose filters are generated by an MLP from interatomic distances expanded in Gaussian radial basis functions. This gives a smooth, twice-differentiable potential energy surface, so forces come as analytic energy gradients, and predictions are rotationally invariant by construction. It became the default baseline and reference implementation for atomistic deep learning for years, and remains the pedagogical entry point to the field.
models.authors: Kristof T. Schütt, Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Huziel E. Sauceda, Stefan Chmiela, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Klaus-Robert Müller
models.paperTitle: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions

keyMetrics.value: state of the art at publication; long-standing standard baseline

models.name: SchNet
models.oneLiner: Continuous-filter convolutions on atom positions — the first broadly reusable deep MLIP/property model
models.description: Replaced the discrete grid filters of standard CNNs with continuous-filter convolutions, so filters are smooth functions of interatomic distance rather than being tied to a lattice — the right inductive bias for atoms at arbitrary positions. Rotationally invariant, energy-conserving, and applicable to both QM9 property regression and MD17 force fields, SchNet became the default architecture and baseline of the late 2010s. Its distance-only (invariant) message passing is precisely the limitation DimeNet (angles) and PaiNN/NequIP (equivariance) were built to overcome.
models.authors: Kristof T. Schütt, Pieter-Jan Kindermans, Huziel E. Sauceda, Stefan Chmiela, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Klaus-Robert Müller
models.paperTitle: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions

models.name: enn-s2s (MPNN)
models.fullName: Message Passing Neural Networks with edge network and set2set readout
models.oneLiner: Unified the GNN zoo into the MPNN framework and beat all hand-crafted descriptors on QM9
models.description: Gilmer et al. showed that graph convolutions, gated graph nets, interaction networks and neural fingerprints are all instances of one abstraction — message passing, update, readout — then searched that design space to find enn-s2s: an edge-network message function with a set2set readout. It reached chemical accuracy on 11 of 13 QM9 targets, decisively ending the descriptor+KRR era and making 'MPNN' the vocabulary of the whole field. The paper's closing argument — that QM9 was near saturation and the field should move to larger molecules and better ground truth — anticipated the next decade.
models.authors: Justin Gilmer, Samuel S. Schoenholz, Patrick F. Riley, Oriol Vinyals, George E. Dahl
models.paperTitle: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

keyMetrics.value: 11 of 13 (average error ratio 0.68; ensemble enn-s2s-ens5: 0.52, U0 0.33)

models.name: qSNAP
models.oneLiner: SNAP extended with quadratic bispectrum terms for large accuracy gains at modest cost
models.description: Extends the SNAP energy model to include quadratic products of bispectrum components, substantially increasing accuracy while keeping the fit linear in its coefficients and the cost only modestly higher. The authors note the structure parallels the embedded atom method, with bispectrum components playing the role of EAM's two-body density functions. It is an early, clean demonstration that the density-trick basis benefits from higher-order products — the same intuition later formalized by ACE.
models.authors: Mitchell A. Wood, Aidan P. Thompson
models.paperTitle: Extending the accuracy of the SNAP interatomic potential form

models.name: wACSF
models.oneLiner: Element-weighted symmetry functions whose count does not grow with the number of species
models.description: Fixes the combinatorial blow-up of standard ACSFs, whose radial/angular function count scales with the number of element pairs and triples. wACSF folds element identity into continuous weighting factors (e.g. nuclear charge) applied inside a single, shared set of symmetry functions, so descriptor dimensionality stays roughly constant as chemical diversity grows. Benchmarked in HDNNPs on QM9 (133,855 molecules, five elements), where wACSFs matched or beat ACSFs with far fewer descriptors. Widely adopted in SchNetPack-adjacent tooling and a conceptual precursor to element-embedding tricks in DPA-1 and other large atomic models.
models.authors: Michael Gastegger, Ludwig Schwiedrzik, Marius Bittermann, Florian Berzsenyi, Philipp Marquetand
models.paperTitle: wACSF — Weighted atom-centered symmetry functions as descriptors in machine learning potentials

models.name: 3D Steerable CNNs
models.oneLiner: SE(3)-equivariant convolutions on volumetric data via an analytic steerable kernel basis
models.description: 3D Steerable CNNs present a convolutional network equivariant to rigid body motions, operating on scalar, vector, and tensor fields over 3D Euclidean space. SE(3)-equivariant convolutions use kernels parameterized as a linear combination of a complete steerable kernel basis derived analytically. Developed concurrently with TFN, it supplied the rigorous representation-theoretic grounding for steerable kernels that e3nn later generalized into a reusable library.
models.authors: Maurice Weiler, Mario Geiger, Max Welling, Wouter Boomsma, Taco S. Cohen
models.paperTitle: 3D Steerable CNNs: Learning Rotationally Equivariant Features in Volumetric Data

models.name: ANI-1x
models.oneLiner: ANI retrained on an actively-sampled dataset — better accuracy from ~25x less data
models.description: Showed that dataset design beats dataset size. Using query-by-committee active learning (ensemble disagreement drives new DFT calculations on normal-mode, MD and dimer sampling), the authors built the ANI-1x dataset of ~5M conformations that outperforms the 20M-conformer random ANI-1 set. The resulting ANI-1x potential is markedly more robust on non-equilibrium and reactive-adjacent geometries. Active learning has since become standard practice across the whole MLIP field, and ANI-1x is the DFT base model from which ANI-1ccx is transfer-learned.
models.authors: Justin S. Smith, Ben Nebgen, Nicholas Lubbers, Olexandr Isayev, Adrian E. Roitberg
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
models.paperTitle: Less is more: Sampling chemical space with active learning

models.name: CGnet
models.oneLiner: First deep-learning coarse-grained force field learned by force matching
models.description: CGnet reformulated coarse-graining as a supervised learning problem, learning a coarse-grained free energy (potential of mean force) by force matching with a neural network subject to physical constraints. It founded the machine-learned coarse-grained force field branch, which is largely absent from atomistic-MLIP timelines despite being the dominant route to ML-accelerated protein and soft-matter simulation.
models.authors: Jiang Wang, Simon Olsson, Christoph Wehmeyer, Adria Perez, Nicholas E. Charron, Gianni de Fabritiis, Frank Noe, Cecilia Clementi
models.paperTitle: Machine Learning of coarse-grained Molecular Dynamics Force Fields

keyMetrics.value: force matching to CG free energy surface

models.name: DeePMD
models.oneLiner: Atomic-energy NNP using local coordinate frames instead of hand-crafted symmetry functions
models.description: Replaced hand-designed symmetry functions with a learned pipeline: each atom's neighbors are mapped into a local reference frame built from the environment itself, and a deep network maps those coordinates to an atomic energy, preserving translation, rotation and permutation symmetry by construction. Achieved ab initio accuracy for water, organics and solids and, crucially, was engineered for production MD — the DeePMD-kit implementation with LAMMPS coupling made large-scale ab initio-quality MD routine and later won a Gordon Bell Prize (100M-atom simulations). Foundation of the entire Deep Potential / DPA ecosystem.
models.authors: Linfeng Zhang, Jiequn Han, Han Wang, Roberto Car, Weinan E
institutions: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Beijing
models.paperTitle: Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics: A Scalable Model with the Accuracy of Quantum Mechanics

models.name: DeepPot-SE
models.oneLiner: End-to-end symmetry-preserving embedding net that removed DeePMD's discontinuous local frames
models.description: Fixed the key defect of original DeePMD — the local reference frames were discontinuous, making the PES non-smooth. DeepPot-SE constructs the descriptor as a learned embedding network acting on smoothed relative coordinates, contracted into a rotationally invariant feature matrix. The result is extensive, continuously differentiable, linear-scaling and fully symmetry-preserving, while being trained end-to-end with no hand-crafted features at all. It works across organic molecules, metals, semiconductors and insulators, and its descriptor (se_e2_a) remains the workhorse of DeePMD-kit and the direct ancestor of DPA-1/2/3.
models.authors: Linfeng Zhang, Jiequn Han, Han Wang, Wissam A. Saidi, Roberto Car, Weinan E
institutions: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Beijing
models.paperTitle: End-to-end Symmetry Preserving Inter-atomic Potential Energy Model for Finite and Extended Systems

models.name: MEGNet
models.oneLiner: Universal graph network with global state variables, covering both molecules and crystals
models.description: Chen, Ye, Zuo, Zheng and Ong adopted DeepMind's graph-network formalism, adding a global state attribute updated alongside node and edge features — which lets one model absorb temperature, pressure or entropy as inputs and enables multi-fidelity band-gap models across DFT functionals. MEGNet beat SchNet on 11 of 13 QM9 properties and set new marks on Materials Project formation energies, band gaps and elastic moduli. It also introduced transfer learning via learned elemental embeddings for data-poor properties. The original TensorFlow repo is archived and superseded by MatGL.
models.authors: Chi Chen, Weike Ye, Yunxing Zuo, Chen Zheng, Shyue Ping Ong
models.paperTitle: Graph Networks as a Universal Machine Learning Framework for Molecules and Crystals

models.name: SOAP-GAP (general-purpose Si)
models.fullName: SOAP-based Gaussian Approximation Potential for Silicon
models.oneLiner: Landmark general-purpose SOAP-GAP covering crystal, liquid, amorphous Si and defects
models.description: The canonical demonstration that SOAP + GAP can produce a single general-purpose potential spanning crystalline, liquid, and amorphous phases plus point, line, and planar defects, rather than one narrow fit per phase. It set the template for how density-trick kernel potentials are trained, validated, and released, and showed the GP posterior variance gives a usable qualitative accuracy estimate per configuration. Widely treated as the reference point for what 'SOAP-GAP' means in practice.
models.authors: Albert P. Bartók, James Kermode, Noam Bernstein, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: Machine learning a general-purpose interatomic potential for silicon

models.name: SchNetPack
models.oneLiner: Open toolbox for atomistic neural networks — training, MD, and benchmark data in one PyTorch package
models.description: SchNetPack packaged the building blocks of atomistic networks (ACSF/wACSF descriptors, SchNet), their training loops, and one-line access to QM9, MD17, ANI-1 and materials datasets into a PyTorch library. It made reproducible atomistic ML practical and is arguably as influential as the SchNet architecture itself. SchNetPack 2.0 (JCP 2023) rebuilt the data pipeline, added equivariant modules such as PaiNN and SO3net, a PyTorch molecular-dynamics engine, and a Hydra/Lightning CLI.
models.authors: Kristof T. Schütt, Pavel Kessel, Michael Gastegger, Kim A. Nicoli, Alexandre Tkatchenko, Klaus-Robert Müller (2.0: Schütt, Hessmann, Gebauer, Lederer, Gastegger)
models.paperTitle: SchNetPack: A Deep Learning Toolbox For Atomistic Systems

models.name: TFN
models.oneLiner: First rotation/translation-equivariant point-cloud network using spherical harmonic filters
models.description: Tensor Field Networks introduced locally equivariant convolutions on 3D point clouds, equivariant to rotations, translations and permutations at every layer. Filters are built from spherical harmonics, so each layer consumes and emits scalars, vectors, and higher-order geometric tensors. This is the foundational paper that established the irreps + Clebsch-Gordan tensor-product design pattern underlying nearly every later E(3)-equivariant MLIP. Rotation equivariance removes the need for orientation data augmentation.
models.authors: Nathaniel Thomas, Tess Smidt, Steven Kearnes, Lusann Yang, Li Li, Kai Kohlhoff, Patrick Riley
models.paperTitle: Tensor field networks: Rotation- and translation-equivariant neural networks for 3D point clouds

models.name: sGDML
models.oneLiner: GDML plus automatically discovered permutational symmetries of the molecule
models.description: sGDML added physical symmetry to GDML by symmetrising the Hessian covariance kernel over the molecule's permutation group, which is recovered automatically from the training data via graph matching across MD frames rather than being specified by hand. Atomic indistinguishability and energy conservation then both hold by construction, cutting the data requirement to a few hundred conformations and making CCSD(T)-quality molecular dynamics practical. It is the kernel-branch counterpart of PIP: same commitment to exact permutation invariance and a global descriptor, different machinery — and the two are now routinely benchmarked head-to-head on systems like H3O2−.
models.authors: Stefan Chmiela, Huziel E. Sauceda, Klaus-Robert Müller, Alexandre Tkatchenko
models.paperTitle: Towards exact molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learned force fields

models.name: ACE
models.oneLiner: Complete body-ordered polynomial expansion of atomic energy; unifies the density branch
models.description: Provides a systematic, complete, and efficiently evaluable expansion of atomic energy in symmetric multi-atom basis functions of arbitrary body order, built by recursive products of density projections. Crucially, the cost of evaluating all basis functions is independent of body order and scales linearly with neighbours — removing the combinatorial blow-up that had capped earlier many-body descriptors. ACE retrospectively unified SOAP, bispectrum/SNAP, and moment-tensor approaches as low-order special cases, and became the theoretical backbone for PACE, GRACE, and MACE. Published directly in PRB with no arXiv preprint.
models.authors: Ralf Drautz
models.paperTitle: Atomic cluster expansion for accurate and transferable interatomic potentials

models.name: AIMNet
models.oneLiner: Multitask, iteratively-refined atomic representation predicting energy, charges and volumes at once
models.description: Bridges the descriptor-sum school and message passing: it starts from ANI-style atomic environment vectors but iteratively refines each atom's "AIM" representation using neighbor charge/state information, effectively a chemically-motivated, few-pass message passing over atomic properties. Trained multitask and multimodal — energies, atomic charges and volumes simultaneously — which both regularizes the representation and gives long-range-aware electrostatics for free. Demonstrated a new axis of transferability: the pretrained AIM representation lets new targets (e.g. solvation free energies) be learned from far less data.
models.authors: Roman Zubatyuk, Justin S. Smith, Jerzy Leszczynski, Olexandr Isayev
models.paperTitle: Accurate and transferable multitask prediction of chemical properties with an atoms-in-molecules neural network

models.name: ANI-1ccx
models.oneLiner: ANI-1x transfer-learned to ~500k CCSD(T)/CBS points — beats DFT at ~1e9x the speed
models.description: The canonical demonstration of Δ-free transfer learning in chemistry: pretrain on 5M cheap DFT conformations (ANI-1x), then fine-tune on ~500k intelligently selected CCSD(T)/CBS points. The resulting general-purpose potential exceeds DFT accuracy on isomerization energies, reaction thermochemistry, drug-like torsion profiles and non-equilibrium forces, at roughly nine orders of magnitude lower cost than the reference method. Established the pretrain-on-cheap/fine-tune-on-gold-standard recipe now used across the MLIP and foundation-model landscape.
models.authors: Justin S. Smith, Benjamin T. Nebgen, Roman Zubatyuk, Nicholas Lubbers, Christian Devereux, Kipton Barros, Sergei Tretiak, Olexandr Isayev, Adrian E. Roitberg
institutions: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
models.paperTitle: Approaching coupled cluster accuracy with a general-purpose neural network potential through transfer learning

models.name: Attentive FP
models.oneLiner: Graph attention with a molecule-level supervirtual node, yielding interpretable fingerprints
models.description: Applies a graph attention mechanism hierarchically — atom-level attention to aggregate neighborhoods, then a molecule-level 'supervirtual node' with recurrent attention readout — to learn a task-specific fingerprint. Its selling point beyond accuracy is interpretability: the attention weights highlight which substructures drive a prediction, and the paper showed the model rediscovers chemically meaningful motifs (e.g. aromaticity, intramolecular effects) without being told. Very widely used in medicinal chemistry and a standard MoleculeNet baseline.
models.authors: Zhaoping Xiong, Dingyan Wang, Xiaohong Liu, Feisheng Zhong, Xiaozhe Wan, Xutong Li, Zhaojun Li, Xiaomin Luo, Kaixian Chen, Hualiang Jiang, Mingyue Zheng
institutions: Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
models.paperTitle: Pushing the Boundaries of Molecular Representation for Drug Discovery with the Graph Attention Mechanism

keyMetrics.value: State-of-the-art at publication across multiple property prediction datasets
Attention weights recover chemically meaningful substructures/motifs

models.name: Chemprop (D-MPNN)
models.oneLiner: Directed-edge MPNN that became the practical standard for drug/materials property prediction
models.description: Passes messages on directed bonds rather than atoms, avoiding the tottering of messages back and forth that plagues naive MPNNs, and crucially combines learned representations with global molecular descriptors (RDKit features). Benchmarked rigorously on 35 datasets with scaffold splits and hyperparameter optimization, it consistently matched or beat fixed-descriptor models. Chemprop matters less for QM9 than for real-world impact: it is the model behind the halicin and abaucin antibiotic discoveries. Chemprop v2 (2023/24) is a full PyTorch-Lightning rewrite for maintainability and extensibility.
models.authors: Kevin Yang, Kyle Swanson, Wengong Jin, Connor Coley, Regina Barzilay, Klavs Jensen, Tommi Jaakkola et al.; v2: Chemprop Development Team (incl. William H. Green)
models.paperTitle: Analyzing Learned Molecular Representations for Property Prediction; Chemprop: A Machine Learning Package for Chemical Property Prediction (v2)
models.venue: J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2019; J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2024 (v2, online 2023)
