Underpinned the halicin and abaucin antibiotic discovery campaigns

models.name: Cormorant
models.oneLiner: Rotationally covariant network for molecular energies using Clebsch-Gordan nonlinearities
models.description: Cormorant is a rotationally covariant neural network architecture for learning the behavior and properties of complex many-body physical systems. Neurons explicitly correspond to subsets of atoms with covariant activations ensuring rotational invariance, and the nonlinearity is based on tensor products and the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition. It targeted two goals: learning atomic potential energy surfaces for MD, and learning DFT ground-state molecular properties. It was among the first to show covariant architectures were competitive on QM9.
models.authors: Brandon M. Anderson, Truong-Son Hy, Risi Kondor
models.paperTitle: Cormorant: Covariant Molecular Neural Networks

keyMetrics.value: competitive with invariant SOTA at the time

models.name: FLARE
models.fullName: Fast Learning of Atomistic Rare Events
models.oneLiner: On-the-fly Bayesian active learning of GP force fields from MD trajectories
models.description: Uses the GP posterior uncertainty to decide, during a running MD simulation, whether to trust the model or call DFT and add the structure to the training set — automating dataset construction instead of curating it up front. The resulting force fields are low-dimensional and interpretable, and can be mapped to fast effective potentials for production MD. FLARE made active learning a standard component of the MLIP workflow and remains a widely used reference implementation. Preprint 2019; published npj Comput. Mater. 2020.
models.authors: Jonathan Vandermause, Steven B. Torrisi, Simon Batzner, Yu Xie, Lixin Sun, Alexie M. Kolpak, Boris Kozinsky
models.paperTitle: On-the-fly active learning of interpretable Bayesian force fields for atomistic rare events

models.name: Fragmented PIP
models.fullName: Fragmented permutationally invariant polynomial PES fitting
models.oneLiner: Fragment the molecule to keep the PIP basis tractable beyond ~10 atoms
models.description: The combinatorial growth of the PIP basis had capped global fits at roughly ten atoms. Qu and Bowman broke the barrier by partitioning a large molecule into fragments, generating PIP bases per fragment plus connecting terms, and keeping permutational invariance and polynomial uniqueness across the partition. Demonstrated on 12-atom N-methyl acetamide with its two methyl rotors, later refined to remove redundant polynomials and accelerate gradients, and pushed to 15-atom acetylacetone and the 44-atom alkane C14H30. This is what keeps the PIP branch competitive on molecules that would otherwise belong exclusively to neural-network potentials.
models.authors: Chen Qu, Joel M. Bowman
models.paperTitle: A fragmented, permutationally invariant polynomial approach for potential energy surfaces of large molecules: Application to N-methyl acetamide

models.name: LODE
models.oneLiner: Density trick applied to a 1/r potential field to capture long-range physics
models.description: Replaces the Gaussian atom density with the scalar potential field generated by neighbouring atoms under an inverse power law, then expands that field in spherical harmonics exactly as SOAP does. This keeps the familiar equivariant density-expansion machinery while encoding electrostatics and dispersion that any strictly local cutoff model structurally cannot represent. LODE opened the long-range subfield within the density branch and directly motivated later latent/Ewald hybrids.
models.authors: Andrea Grisafi, Michele Ceriotti
models.paperTitle: Incorporating long-range physics in atomic-scale machine learning

models.name: PhysNet
models.oneLiner: Message-passing net predicting energies, forces, dipoles and partial charges with explicit electrostatics
models.description: Unke and Meuwly argued that purely local neural potentials cannot describe charge transfer or long-range interactions, and built a modular residual message-passing architecture that outputs atomic energies plus partial charges, then adds explicit Coulomb electrostatics and Grimme D3 dispersion analytically. Charges are corrected to conserve total molecular charge and are trained against dipole moments rather than arbitrary population analyses. It set state of the art on QM9, MD17 and ISO17 and introduced datasets probing reactions and condensed-phase behavior, making the case that physics-based long-range terms are not optional.
models.authors: Oliver T. Unke, Markus Meuwly
models.paperTitle: PhysNet: A Neural Network for Predicting Energies, Forces, Dipole Moments and Partial Charges

keyMetrics.value: state of the art at publication

models.name: SALTED
models.fullName: Symmetry-Adapted Learning of Three-dimensional Electron Densities
models.oneLiner: Symmetry-adapted GPR for the electron density expanded on atom-centered basis functions
models.description: SALTED learns the all-electron density as an equivariant field decomposed onto atom-centered spherical-harmonic basis functions using symmetry-adapted Gaussian process regression, and extends to electrostatic response properties. Growing out of the SOAP/lambda-SOAP lineage, it is the canonical kernel-based electron-density learning framework and a direct ancestor of modern equivariant field-prediction models.
models.authors: Andrea Grisafi, Alberto Fabrizio, Alan M. Lewis, Benjamin Meyer, Mariana Rossi, Clemence Corminboeuf, Michele Ceriotti
institutions: Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter
models.paperTitle: Transferable Machine-Learning Model of the Electron Density

keyMetrics.value: electron density on atom-centered spherical harmonic basis

models.name: TeaNet
models.oneLiner: Graph conv net propagating rank>=2 tensors, inspired by iterative electronic relaxation
models.description: TeaNet is a deep graph convolution architecture whose message passing propagates rank >= 2 Cartesian tensor information between atoms, explicitly designed to mimic the iterative electronic relaxation of a tight-binding/bond-order picture. It is an important and often-overlooked early Cartesian-tensor equivariant network, predating NequIP, and it is the architecture underlying the commercial PFP universal potential.
models.authors: So Takamoto, Satoshi Izumi, Ju Li
models.paperTitle: TeaNet: universal neural network interatomic potential inspired by iterative electronic relaxations

keyMetrics.value: first 18 elements of the periodic table

models.name: aPIP
models.oneLiner: PIPs recast as atom-centred, explicitly body-ordered site energies for materials
models.description: van der Oord, Dusson, Csányi and Ortner transplanted the PIP idea from molecular PESs to condensed-matter interatomic potentials by decomposing the total energy into atom-centred contributions expanded in explicitly body-ordered permutation-invariant polynomials, with each order regularised separately. The explicit body-order decomposition keeps the dimensionality of each term low (about 10 even for five-body) and makes the fit interpretable, since 2-, 3- and 4-body physics can be inspected independently — unlike kernel or neural models. Despite the folk wisdom that polynomials extrapolate badly, the regularised fits transferred better than GAP, and the work is a direct conceptual bridge from the Bowman/Braams PIP tradition to the ACE framework.
models.authors: Cas van der Oord, Geneviève Dusson, Gábor Csányi, Christoph Ortner
models.paperTitle: Regularised atomic body-ordered permutation-invariant polynomials for the construction of interatomic potentials

models.name: 4G-HDNNP
models.oneLiner: HDNNP + CENT-style global charge equilibration: non-local charge transfer and multiple charge states
models.description: Merges the two branches of the Behler school: atomic NNs predict environment-dependent electronegativities that feed a global charge-equilibration step (as in CENT), and the resulting charges are then fed back as non-local inputs to the short-range atomic NNs that produce atomic energies. This closes 2G/3G's fundamental blind spot — systems where the electronic structure depends on distant atoms (charged defects, external fields, multiple charge states, long-range charge transfer) — while retaining accurate local bonding. Now the reference architecture for charge-aware MLIPs; subsequent work targets its O(N^3)/O(N^2) equilibration bottleneck via iterative and particle-mesh QEq solvers.
models.authors: Tsz Wai Ko, Jonas A. Finkler, Stefan Goedecker, Jörg Behler
models.paperTitle: A fourth-generation high-dimensional neural network potential with accurate electrostatics including non-local charge transfer

models.name: AIMNet-NSE
models.fullName: Atoms-in-Molecules Neural Network with Neural Spin Equilibration
models.oneLiner: First NNP to predict energies for arbitrary combinations of molecular charge and spin multiplicity
models.description: AIMNet-NSE broke the long-standing architectural limitation that neural network potentials were parameterized only for neutral molecules or closed-shell ions. By introducing neural spin equilibration, it predicts molecular energies for arbitrary combinations of total charge and spin multiplicity to ~2-3 kcal/mol, and spin-charges to ~0.01e, for small and medium organic molecules. Crucially it bypasses QM entirely to derive ionization potentials, electron affinities, and conceptual-DFT quantities (electronegativity, hardness, condensed Fukui functions), establishing the charge/spin-conditioning paradigm that AIMNet2, AIMNet2-NSE, OMol25/eSEN, UMA, and OrbMol all later adopted.
models.authors: Roman Zubatyuk, Justin S. Smith, Benjamin T. Nebgen, Sergei Tretiak, Olexandr Isayev
models.paperTitle: Teaching a neural network to attach and detach electrons from molecules

keyMetrics.value: IP, EA, electronegativity, hardness, Fukui functions without QM

models.name: ANI-2x / ANI-2xt
models.oneLiner: Seven-element (HCNOFSCl) transferable NNP covering ~90% of drug-like chemical space
models.description: ANI-2x extended the ANI family from H/C/N/O to also include S, F, and Cl — seven elements that together cover roughly 90% of drug-like molecules — and added torsional refinement training to fix the torsion-profile errors that made earlier ANI models unusable for conformational work. It is built on Behler-Parrinello-style atomic environment vectors with per-element feed-forward networks and ensembling, and remains the most-cited pre-foundation-era organic NNP and the baseline every subsequent molecular MLIP reports against. ANI-2xt is the tautomer-refined variant, trained on a tautomer-rich dataset, which cuts tautomeric reaction energy error by 42% versus ANI-2x against CCSD(T) references. Both remain widely available through TorchANI and OpenMM-ML.
models.authors: Christian Devereux, Justin S. Smith, Kate K. Davis, Kipton Barros, Roman Zubatyuk, Olexandr Isayev, Adrian E. Roitberg
models.paperTitle: Extending the Applicability of the ANI Deep Learning Molecular Potential to Sulfur and Halogens

keyMetrics.value: H, C, N, O, F, S, Cl (~90% of drug-like molecules)

models.name: ChemBERTa / ChemBERTa-2
models.oneLiner: RoBERTa-style masked language model over SMILES strings for molecular property prediction
models.description: Treats SMILES as a language and applies the BERT/RoBERTa recipe: masked-token pretraining on up to 77M PubChem SMILES, then fine-tuning for property prediction. ChemBERTa established that chemical language models scale with pretraining data and that attention maps recover chemically sensible structure, while being frank that it did not yet beat strong graph models. ChemBERTa-2 pushed toward a 'chemical foundation model', comparing masked-LM against multi-task regression pretraining and studying scaling. Its main legacy is accessibility — a HuggingFace-native, easily fine-tuned baseline that made molecular ML approachable.
models.authors: Seyone Chithrananda, Gabriel Grand, Bharath Ramsundar; ChemBERTa-2: Walid Ahmad, Elana Simon, Seyone Chithrananda, Gabriel Grand, Bharath Ramsundar
models.paperTitle: ChemBERTa: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Pretraining for Molecular Property Prediction; ChemBERTa-2: Towards Chemical Foundation Models

keyMetrics.value: Competitive with, but generally not exceeding, strong graph baselines

models.name: DeePKS
models.oneLiner: Machine-learned self-consistent correction functional reaching chemical accuracy
models.description: DeePKS learns a neural correction to a baseline exchange-correlation functional built on local descriptors of the projected density matrix, applied self-consistently within the Kohn-Sham loop to reach chemical accuracy at near Hartree-Fock cost. With its perturbative variant DeePHF, it is the main deep-learning-functional line from the DeepModeling ecosystem and a distinct alternative to DM21 in the machine-learned-DFT branch.
models.authors: Yixiao Chen, Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang, Weinan E
institutions: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Beijing
models.paperTitle: DeePKS: A Comprehensive Data-Driven Approach toward Chemically Accurate Density Functional Theory
models.venue: J. Chem. Theory Comput. 17(1), 170-181 (2021); precursor J. Phys. Chem. A 124(35), 7155 (2020)

models.name: DeepDFT
models.oneLiner: Message-passing model predicting the full electron density on a real-space grid
models.description: Rather than regressing a scalar property, DeepDFT predicts the *electron density* itself — the fundamental object of DFT from which, by Hohenberg-Kohn, all ground-state properties follow. It treats grid points as special probe nodes in a message-passing graph over atoms, so density is queried at arbitrary points in space with the right invariances. Reported errors are smaller than the spread between different exchange-correlation functionals, meaning the ML error is below functional-choice ambiguity. Useful as an SCF initial guess and a step toward learning electronic structure rather than fitting endpoints.
models.authors: Peter Bjørn Jørgensen, Arghya Bhowmik
models.paperTitle: DeepDFT: Neural Message Passing Network for Accurate Charge Density Prediction

keyMetrics.value: Prediction error lower than the variation between different XC functionals

models.name: DimeNet / DimeNet++
models.oneLiner: Adds bond angles via directional messages on spherical Bessel/harmonic bases
models.description: Diagnosed the core weakness of SchNet-style models: distance-only messages cannot distinguish configurations differing in bond angles. DimeNet passes messages between *directed edges* (atom pairs) rather than atoms, embedding the angle between adjacent bonds in a basis of spherical Bessel functions and spherical harmonics — a physically-principled, rotationally-equivariant orthogonal basis that is far more parameter-efficient than Gaussian radial bases. DimeNet++ then made it ~8x faster with a slimmer architecture and better accuracy. This established angular/directional information as essential, a line continued by GemNet and SphereNet (which reached 22.8 meV HOMO / 6.26 meV U0).
models.authors: Johannes Gasteiger (Klicpera), Janek Groß, Stephan Günnemann; with Shankari Giri and Johannes T. Margraf (DimeNet++)
models.paperTitle: Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs (DimeNet); Fast and Uncertainty-Aware Directional Message Passing for Non-Equilibrium Molecules (DimeNet++)

models.name: DimeNet++
models.oneLiner: Faster, more accurate DimeNet plus the COLL non-equilibrium dataset and uncertainty estimates
models.description: A targeted efficiency rework of DimeNet: the costly bilinear interaction layer is replaced, embeddings are down-projected before the expensive angular step, and depth is traded for width. The result is 8x faster and 10% more accurate on QM9. The paper also released COLL — distorted small-molecule configurations sampled from molecular collisions — to test far-from-equilibrium reactive regimes that QM9-style benchmarks ignore, and studied ensembles and mean-variance estimation for uncertainty-guided exploration. DimeNet++ was the practical workhorse and a standard OC20 baseline.
models.authors: Johannes Klicpera (Gasteiger), Shankari Giri, Johannes T. Margraf, Stephan Günnemann
models.paperTitle: Fast and Uncertainty-Aware Directional Message Passing for Non-Equilibrium Molecules

models.name: Espaloma
models.fullName: Extensible Surrogate Potential Optimized by Message-passing Algorithms
models.oneLiner: GNN replaces discrete atom typing; end-to-end differentiable MM force field construction
models.description: Espaloma's insight is that the discrete, hand-written atom-typing rules at the heart of every classical force field are the real bottleneck - and they can be replaced by a graph neural network that maps the chemical graph to continuous atom embeddings, then pools them into bond, angle, and torsion parameters in a symmetry-consistent way. Because the whole pipeline is differentiable in the GNN weights, parameters can be optimized end-to-end against QM energies/forces or condensed-phase data. Critically, the output is still a standard MM force field - it runs at classical MD speed in OpenMM. This is the cleanest bridge between the classical and ML branches: ML for parameterization, classical physics for evaluation.
models.authors: Yuanqing Wang, Josh Fass, Benjamin Kaminow, John E. Herr, Dominic Rufa, Ivy Zhang, Iván Pulido, Mike Henry, John D. Chodera
models.paperTitle: End-to-end differentiable construction of molecular mechanics force fields

models.name: GM-NN
models.oneLiner: Invariant descriptors from Gaussian-weighted geometric moments contracted in Cartesian form, fed to an MLP.
models.description: Zaverkin and Kästner replaced hand-tuned ACSF symmetry functions with 'Gaussian moments': radial Gaussians weighted by outer products of normalized distance vectors, i.e. Cartesian geometric moments of the atomic density. Full tensor contractions of these moments give a compact, systematically extendable invariant descriptor that encodes both central and neighbor species. Because everything is expressed as pairwise distance vectors plus tensor contractions, the descriptor maps very efficiently onto GPUs. This is essentially the MTP density trick recast as a neural-network descriptor.
models.authors: Viktor Zaverkin, Johannes Kästner
models.paperTitle: Gaussian Moments as Physically Inspired Molecular Descriptors for Accurate and Scalable Machine Learning Potentials

models.name: GROVER
models.fullName: Graph Representation frOm self-superVised mEssage passing tRansformer
models.oneLiner: Self-supervised GNN-Transformer hybrid pretrained on 10M unlabeled molecules
models.description: Tackled molecular ML's central bottleneck — labels are scarce and expensive, unlabeled molecules are abundant. GROVER couples message-passing GNNs with a Transformer backbone and pretrains on ~10M unlabeled molecules using self-supervised tasks at both node/edge level (contextual property prediction) and graph level (motif prediction), then fine-tunes. With ~100M parameters it was among the largest molecular models of its time and demonstrated that the NLP pretraining recipe transfers to molecular graphs — a thesis later pursued by MolCLR (contrastive, Nat. Mach. Intell. 2022), GEM (geometry-enhanced), and 3D-Infomax (2D/3D mutual information).
models.authors: Yu Rong, Yatao Bian, Tingyang Xu, Weiyang Xie, Ying Wei, Wenbing Huang, Junzhou Huang
models.paperTitle: Self-Supervised Graph Transformer on Large-Scale Molecular Data

keyMetrics.value: Large gains over non-pretrained baselines at publication

models.name: MLIP-2
models.fullName: MLIP package: Moment Tensor Potentials with MPI and Active Learning
models.oneLiner: Reference MTP implementation with MPI parallelism, LAMMPS interface and D-optimal active learning.
models.description: The MLIP package turned moment tensor potentials into a practical production tool. It provides MPI-parallel training and evaluation, a LAMMPS interface, and — most importantly — active learning based on a D-optimality (MaxVol) criterion over the linear MTP basis, which yields a cheap, principled extrapolation grade for on-the-fly training-set selection. The paper is written as a tutorial showing how to sample configurations, how error scales with training-set size, and how to run ab initio calculations cost-effectively. The D-optimal active learning scheme became a widely copied idea across the MLIP field.
models.authors: Ivan S. Novikov, Konstantin Gubaev, Evgeny V. Podryabinkin, Alexander V. Shapeev
institutions: Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology
models.paperTitle: The MLIP package: moment tensor potentials with MPI and active learning

models.name: NICE
models.oneLiner: Recursive construction of high-body-order equivariants with automatic feature contraction
models.description: Exploits recursion relations between equivariant features of different orders so that high-body-order terms can be built by iteratively combining lower-order ones, rather than enumerated combinatorially. An automatic contraction step prunes the exponentially growing feature space down to the most informative directions at each order, keeping cost manageable. NICE is the Ceriotti-group counterpart to ACE's recursive philosophy and a key link between the SOAP density expansion and modern equivariant architectures. The reference implementation was archived in January 2026.
models.authors: Jigyasa Nigam, Sergey Pozdnyakov, Michele Ceriotti
models.paperTitle: Recursive evaluation and iterative contraction of N-body equivariant features

models.name: OrbNet / OrbNet-Denali
models.oneLiner: GNN over symmetry-adapted atomic-orbital features from a cheap tight-binding calculation
models.description: Instead of learning from raw geometry, OrbNet runs a cheap semi-empirical (GFN-xTB) calculation and feeds its symmetry-adapted atomic-orbital feature matrices (Fock, density, overlap) into a graph network — a Δ-learning scheme where the features themselves already carry quantum-mechanical information. This gives outstanding data efficiency and transferability, since electronic structure rather than the network must generalize. OrbNet-Denali scaled it to a general-purpose model for biological and organic chemistry (trained on ~2.3M conformers), delivering DFT-level accuracy at semi-empirical cost. Developed commercially at Entos/Iambic Therapeutics.
models.authors: Zhuoran Qiao, Matthew Welborn, Anima Anandkumar, Frederick R. Manby, Thomas F. Miller III; Denali: Anders S. Christensen, Sai Krishna Sirumalla et al.
models.paperTitle: OrbNet: Deep learning for quantum chemistry using symmetry-adapted atomic-orbital features; OrbNet Denali: A machine learning potential for biological and organic chemistry with semi-empirical cost and DFT accuracy
models.venue: J. Chem. Phys. 2020; J. Chem. Phys. 2021 (Denali)

keyMetrics.benchmark: Downstream molecular datasets (QM7b-T, QM9, GDB-13-T, DrugBank-T)
keyMetrics.value: Outperforms prior ML models at greatly reduced cost; strong out-of-distribution transfer
~2.3M conformers of biological/organic molecules; DFT accuracy at semi-empirical cost

models.name: SE(3)-Transformer
models.oneLiner: Self-attention module for 3D point clouds equivariant under continuous roto-translations
models.description: The SE(3)-Transformer is a variant of self-attention for 3D point clouds and graphs that is equivariant under continuous 3D roto-translations. It combines the benefits of attention (handling large, variable-size point sets) with guaranteed SE(3) equivariance, and a positive corollary of equivariance is increased weight-tying within the model. Evaluated on an N-body toy simulation, ScanObjectNN and QM9, it outperformed both a strong non-equivariant attention baseline and an equivariant model without attention. It established equivariant attention as a design family later scaled up by Equiformer.
models.authors: Fabian B. Fuchs, Daniel E. Worrall, Volker Fischer, Max Welling
models.paperTitle: SE(3)-Transformers: 3D Roto-Translation Equivariant Attention Networks

models.name: SchNarc
models.oneLiner: SchNet adapted to multiple electronic states for ML-driven nonadiabatic photodynamics
models.description: Couples SchNet to the SHARC surface-hopping dynamics code to predict everything photodynamics needs — energies and forces for *multiple* electronic states, plus nonadiabatic and spin-orbit couplings. The hard part is that excited-state surfaces cross (conical intersections) and coupling signs are arbitrary, so the paper introduces phase-correction and diagonalization strategies to make the targets learnable. It enabled nanosecond-scale photodynamics that are computationally impossible with on-the-fly quantum chemistry, extending ML from ground-state properties into excited-state and spectroscopic prediction (a lineage also including PaiNN's IR/Raman spectra and ML NMR shift predictors).
models.authors: Julia Westermayr, Michael Gastegger, Philipp Marquetand
models.paperTitle: Combining SchNet and SHARC: The SchNarc Machine Learning Approach for Excited-State Dynamics

keyMetrics.value: Nanosecond-scale nonadiabatic dynamics, infeasible for on-the-fly quantum chemistry
Multi-state energies, forces, nonadiabatic couplings, spin-orbit couplings

models.name: TorchANI
models.oneLiner: PyTorch reimplementation of ANI — autograd forces/Hessians, the field's most-used NNP reference code
models.description: Reimplemented the ANI stack (AEV computation and atomic networks) purely in PyTorch operators, replacing the original C++/CUDA NeuroChem. Because every step is a differentiable tensor op, forces and Hessians come free from autograd and force training needs no extra code — a decisive usability win that made ANI the standard teaching and prototyping NNP. Trades some raw speed for readability, portability and hackability. TorchANI 2.0 continues under Roitberg-group maintenance and ships ANI-1x, ANI-1ccx and ANI-2x weights.
models.authors: Xiang Gao, Farhad Ramezanghorbani, Olexandr Isayev, Justin S. Smith, Adrian E. Roitberg
models.paperTitle: TorchANI: A Free and Open Source PyTorch-Based Deep Learning Implementation of the ANI Neural Network Potentials

models.name: Δ-ML PIP
models.fullName: Δ-Machine Learning with permutationally invariant polynomials
models.oneLiner: PIP-fit the DFT-to-CCSD(T) correction, buying gold-standard accuracy for ~200 CC energies
models.description: Nandi, Qu, Houston, Conte and Bowman fit a PIP surface not to the energy but to the difference between a cheap DFT-based PES and coupled-cluster reference energies. Because the correction surface is smooth and low-amplitude, it needs drastically less high-level data: as few as 200 CCSD(T) energies lifted PESs for CH4, H3O+ and N-methyl acetamide to benchmark accuracy. The idea generalises across the branch — a CCSD(T) 4-body Δ-correction was applied to MB-pol, PIP-NN Δ-ML was used for HO2 self-reaction dynamics, and the approach has since produced transferable gold-standard alkane potentials.
models.authors: Apurba Nandi, Chen Qu, Paul L. Houston, Riccardo Conte, Joel M. Bowman
models.paperTitle: Δ-machine learning for potential energy surfaces: A PIP approach to bring a DFT-based PES to CCSD(T) level of theory

models.name: ALIGNN
models.oneLiner: Alternating message passing on the bond graph and its line graph to encode bond angles
models.description: Choudhary and DeCost included angular information in a way orthogonal to DimeNet's: build the line graph of the atomistic bond graph (nodes = bonds, edges = bond triplets carrying angles) and alternate edge-gated convolutions between the two graphs. This composes cleanly with existing crystal-graph machinery and improved accuracy by up to 85% over prior GNNs at comparable training speed. Its reach came from breadth — NIST released ALIGNN models for 52 properties spanning JARVIS-DFT, Materials Project and QM9, making it a workhorse for high-throughput materials screening.
models.authors: Kamal Choudhary, Brian DeCost
models.paperTitle: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network for improved materials property predictions

models.name: CDVAE
models.oneLiner: First diffusion-based generative model for periodic crystal structures
models.description: CDVAE generates periodic materials by encoding to a latent space and decoding through a diffusion process that moves atomic coordinates toward lower-energy configurations, while respecting permutation, translation, rotation, and periodic invariances. It established diffusion-based crystal generation and is the direct ancestor of MatterGen and the DiffCSP line, making it a necessary parent node for the generative branch of the tree.
models.authors: Tian Xie, Xiang Fu, Octavian-Eugen Ganea, Regina Barzilay, Tommi Jaakkola
models.paperTitle: Crystal Diffusion Variational Autoencoder for Periodic Material Generation

keyMetrics.value: first diffusion decoder for periodic crystal generation

models.name: DM21
models.oneLiner: Neural exchange-correlation functional that fixes delocalization and static-correlation errors
models.description: Rather than surrogating DFT, DM21 replaces its unknown component: the exchange-correlation functional is a neural network trained on molecular data plus, crucially, fictitious systems with fractional electron charge and fractional spin. Those fractional-electron constraints directly target the two pathologies that have limited DFT for decades — delocalization error and static correlation error — which hand-crafted functionals systematically violate. Published in Science, DM21 showed that ML can improve the *physics* inside a first-principles method, not merely imitate its outputs, and it opened the learned-functional line continued by Skala.
models.authors: James Kirkpatrick, Brendan McMorrow, David H. P. Turban, Alexander L. Gaunt, James S. Spencer, Alexander G. D. G. Matthews, Annette Obika, Louis Thiry, Meire Fortunato, David Pfau, Aron J. Cohen et al.
models.paperTitle: Pushing the frontiers of density functionals by solving the fractional electron problem

keyMetrics.value: State-of-the-art at publication; correct behavior on fractional charge/spin systems
Resolves failure modes systematically present in hand-designed functionals

models.name: EGNN
models.oneLiner: E(n)-equivariance with no spherical harmonics — just coordinates and distances
models.description: Showed that equivariance to rotations, translations, reflections and permutations can be obtained without any spherical harmonics or higher-order representations: update coordinates along relative-position vectors weighted by learned scalar functions of distance. The result is strikingly simple, scales to arbitrary dimension n, and is fast. Accuracy on QM9 trails DimeNet++/PaiNN, but its simplicity made it the default backbone for a huge amount of downstream work — especially generative modeling (E(3) diffusion for molecule generation) rather than pure regression.
models.authors: Victor Garcia Satorras, Emiel Hoogeboom, Max Welling
models.paperTitle: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

models.name: GM-NN (2021)
models.fullName: Fast and Sample-Efficient Interatomic Neural Network Potentials Based on Gaussian Moments
models.oneLiner: Improved GM-NN architecture: better accuracy, far shorter training, extended to periodic systems.
models.description: A substantially revised GM-NN architecture with an improved network design, trainable scaling/shifting of atomic energies, and better initialization, giving higher accuracy with markedly reduced training times. It extends Gaussian-moment potentials from molecules to periodic solids, making the approach applicable to materials as well as chemistry. This version is the one typically benchmarked against SchNet, PhysNet and GAP, and it anchors the Stuttgart/NEC line of work that later produced the irreducible Cartesian tensor message-passing models.
models.authors: Viktor Zaverkin, David Holzmüller, Ingo Steinwart, Johannes Kästner
models.paperTitle: Fast and Sample-Efficient Interatomic Neural Network Potentials for Molecules and Materials Based on Gaussian Moments

models.name: GemNet
models.oneLiner: Universal approximator via two-hop directed message passing with dihedral (four-body) interactions
models.description: Gasteiger, Becker and Günnemann proved that GNNs with directed edge embeddings and two-hop message passing are universal approximators for rotation-equivariant, permutation-invariant predictions — a theoretical guarantee that distance-only and even angle-only nets lack. GemNet realizes this with quadruplet interactions encoding dihedral angles. The paper's GemNet-Q (quadruplet) and GemNet-T (triplet-only) variants, each in direct-force (-dT) or energy-gradient flavors, became standard: GemNet-dT predicts forces directly as a non-conservative output for large-scale speed, trading energy conservation for throughput on OC20.
models.authors: Johannes Gasteiger, Florian Becker, Stephan Günnemann
models.paperTitle: GemNet: Universal Directional Graph Neural Networks for Molecules

models.name: Graphormer
models.oneLiner: Standard Transformer + structural encodings; won the OGB-LSC PCQM4M quantum chemistry track
models.description: Answered 'Do Transformers really perform bad for graph representation?' with a decisive no: a vanilla Transformer plus three structural encodings — centrality (degree) encoding, spatial encoding via shortest-path distance as an attention bias, and edge encoding — outperforms message-passing GNNs. It won the KDD Cup 2021 OGB Large-Scale Challenge on PCQM4M, proving that at large data scale, generic attention with the right positional priors beats bespoke chemistry architectures. Graphormer is the direct ancestor of Transformer-M and Uni-Mol+.
models.authors: Chengxuan Ying, Tianle Cai, Shengjie Luo, Shuxin Zheng, Guolin Ke, Di He, Yanming Shen, Tie-Yan Liu
models.paperTitle: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?

keyMetrics.value: Winner, KDD Cup 2021 OGB-LSC quantum chemistry track (prev. SOTA GIN-VN 0.1395 eV)

models.name: Linear ACE
models.fullName: Linear Atomic Cluster Expansion Force Fields for Organic Molecules
models.oneLiner: Four/five-body linear ACE for organic molecules, evaluated beyond RMSE
models.description: Shows that purely linear ACE models with four- or five-body symmetric polynomial basis functions improve on empirical force fields by up to a factor of ten and match contemporary neural-network accuracy, at a fraction of the cost and with a convex fit. Equally influential is its methodological argument that RMSE alone is a poor proxy for force-field quality, pushing the field toward physically meaningful validation (barriers, dimer curves, MD stability). A key demonstration that the density branch did not need deep learning to be competitive on molecules. Preprint on ChemRxiv, not arXiv.
models.authors: Dávid Péter Kovács, Cas van der Oord, Jiri Kucera, Alice E. A. Allen, Daniel J. Cole, Christoph Ortner, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: Linear Atomic Cluster Expansion Force Fields for Organic Molecules: Beyond RMSE

models.name: MALA
models.oneLiner: Predicts the local density of states to reconstruct DFT observables at scale
models.description: MALA learns the local density of states (LDOS) from local atomic descriptors, from which total energy, electron density, and DOS are then reconstructed, giving a surrogate for finite-temperature Kohn-Sham DFT that scales linearly and reaches systems of 100k+ atoms. It is the leading representative of the 'learn the electronic structure, derive everything else' strategy, distinct from both direct MLIPs and Hamiltonian learning.
models.authors: J. A. Ellis, L. Fiedler, A. Cangi, S. Rajamanickam, A. P. Thompson, N. A. Modine
models.paperTitle: Accelerating finite-temperature Kohn-Sham density functional theory with deep neural networks

models.name: MoLFormer-XL
models.oneLiner: 1.1B-SMILES chemical language model with rotary embeddings and linear attention
models.description: Scaled chemical language modeling far beyond ChemBERTa: pretrained on 1.1 billion SMILES from PubChem and ZINC using rotary position embeddings and linear attention to make sequences that long tractable. The headline finding is that a model reading only 1D strings — never given a graph or 3D coordinates — nonetheless learns representations that encode molecular structure and even recover interatomic spatial relationships, and competes with or beats graph neural networks on property benchmarks. Strong evidence that scale can substitute for architectural inductive bias in chemistry.
models.authors: Jerret Ross, Brian Belgodere, Vijil Chenthamarakshan, Inkit Padhi, Youssef Mroueh, Payel Das
models.paperTitle: Large-scale chemical language representations capture molecular structure and properties

keyMetrics.value: Competitive with or superior to graph-based models on several tasks
Learned attention recovers molecular structure/spatial relationships from 1D strings alone

models.name: MolCLR
models.oneLiner: SimCLR-style contrastive pretraining on 10M molecular graphs via chemically-aware augmentations
models.description: Adapts contrastive learning to molecular graphs with three augmentations — atom masking, bond deletion and subgraph removal — pulling together augmented views of the same molecule and pushing apart different ones, over ~10M unlabeled molecules. The contribution is largely in identifying which augmentations preserve chemical semantics, since standard image augmentations have no molecular analogue. Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, it became the reference point for contrastive molecular pretraining, alongside GEM (geometry-enhanced, Nat. Mach. Intell. 2022) and 3D-Infomax (ICML 2022), which instead distills 3D information into a 2D encoder via mutual-information maximization so 3D is needed only at pretraining time.
models.authors: Yuyang Wang, Jianren Wang, Zhonglin Cao, Amir Barati Farimani
models.paperTitle: Molecular contrastive learning of representations via graph neural networks

keyMetrics.value: Consistent gains over supervised-only GNN baselines

models.name: NEP
models.oneLiner: Chebyshev/Legendre-descriptor NNP trained by evolution strategy, GPU-native in GPUMD
models.description: An unusual and very pragmatic corner of the descriptor-sum branch: a single-hidden-layer network on a compact descriptor built from Chebyshev (radial) and Legendre (angular) polynomial expansions, trained not by backpropagation but by the separable natural evolution strategy (SNES). Combined with a from-scratch GPU implementation in GPUMD, this yields near-empirical-potential throughput while retaining above-average ML accuracy — making NEP the tool of choice for very large, very long MD (thermal transport, amorphous materials, phonons). Successive versions NEP2/NEP3/NEP4 improved multi-component accuracy and generality; qNEP adds dynamic charges and TNEP handles tensorial targets.
models.authors: Zheyong Fan, Zezhu Zeng, Cunzhi Zhang, Yanzhou Wang, Keke Song, Haikuan Dong, Yue Chen, Tapio Ala-Nissila
models.paperTitle: Neuroevolution machine learning potentials: Combining high accuracy and low cost in atomistic simulations and application to heat transport

keyMetrics.value: far more efficient at comparable accuracy

models.name: NequIP
models.oneLiner: E(3)-equivariant MPNN interatomic potential with extreme data efficiency
models.description: NequIP is the model that brought E(3)-equivariance decisively into interatomic potentials. Where contemporary symmetry-aware models used invariant convolutions acting only on scalars, NequIP employs E(3)-equivariant convolutions for interactions of geometric tensors, giving a more information-rich and faithful representation of atomic environments. It reached state-of-the-art accuracy across diverse molecules and materials while using up to three orders of magnitude fewer training data, directly challenging the belief that deep networks need massive training sets. It is the direct ancestor of Allegro, SevenNet, and Nequix.
models.authors: Simon Batzner, Albert Musaelian, Lixin Sun, Mario Geiger, Jonathan P. Mailoa, Mordechai Kornbluth, Nicola Molinari, Tess E. Smidt, Boris Kozinsky
institutions: Robert Bosch Research and Technology Center
models.paperTitle: E(3)-equivariant graph neural networks for data-efficient and accurate interatomic potentials

keyMetrics.value: state of the art at publication

models.name: OPLS4
models.fullName: Optimized Potentials for Liquid Simulations, version 4
models.oneLiner: Schrödinger's commercial OPLS successor targeting charged species and sulfur chemistry
models.description: OPLS4 builds on OPLS3/OPLS3e with a novel parameterization strategy for molecular ions and improved coverage of sulfur-containing moieties - two regimes where earlier fixed-charge force fields degraded badly on drug-like chemical space. It couples an enormous proprietary torsion database with automated on-the-fly parameter generation, and reports improved accuracy on small-molecule solvation and protein-ligand binding free energy benchmarks. It represents the high-water mark of the industrial, data-heavy but still rule-and-lookup-based classical FF, in direct contrast to the open GNN-parameterized approaches emerging in parallel.
models.authors: Chao Lu, Chuanjie Wu, Delaram Ghoreishi, Wei Chen, Lingle Wang, Wolfgang Damm, Gregory A. Ross, Manoj K. Dahlgren, Ellery Russell, Christopher D. Von Bargen, Robert Abel, Richard A. Friesner, Edward D. Harder
models.paperTitle: OPLS4: Improving Force Field Accuracy on Challenging Regimes of Chemical Space

models.name: OpenFF (Parsley / Sage / Rosemary)
models.fullName: Open Force Field Initiative force fields
models.oneLiner: Open, direct-chemical-perception force fields using SMIRNOFF SMARTS typing instead of atom types
models.description: The Open Force Field Initiative rebuilt small-molecule force field science as open software and open data. Its central technical move is SMIRNOFF: parameters are assigned by direct chemical perception from SMARTS patterns applied to the molecular graph, eliminating the brittle discrete atom-typing layer of GAFF and making the whole parameter set differentiable-adjacent and systematically refittable against QM plus experimental physical property data. Parsley (1.x) was the first release; Sage (2.0.0, 2023) refit valence and vdW parameters together; Rosemary (3.0.0) will unify small molecules with proteins under one transferable parameter set and remains at alpha as of the openff-3.0.0-alpha0 research release (Oct 2025), with native PTM support in development.
models.authors: Simon Boothroyd, Pavan Kumar Behara, Owen C. Madin, David F. Hahn, Hyesu Jang, Vytautas Gapsys, Jeffrey R. Wagner, Joshua T. Horton, David L. Dotson, Lee-Ping Wang, Daniel J. Cole, Michael K. Gilson, John D. Chodera, Christopher I. Bayly, Michael R. Shirts, David L. Mobley
models.paperTitle: Development and Benchmarking of Open Force Field 2.0.0: The Sage Small Molecule Force Field

models.name: PACE
models.fullName: Performant implementation of the Atomic Cluster Expansion
models.oneLiner: Fast C++ ACE implementation plus pacemaker fitting; ACE made production-ready
models.description: Delivers ACE as an optimized C++ evaluator suitable for large-scale atomistic simulation, with LAMMPS integration and the companion `pacemaker` fitting toolchain. Demonstrated on copper and silicon, it showed ACE could sit on a strong accuracy-versus-speed Pareto front relative to both kernel methods and neural networks of the era. PACE is the practical vehicle through which most of the materials community actually uses ACE, and the software lineage that later became GRACE.
models.authors: Yury Lysogorskiy, Cas van der Oord, Anton Bochkarev, Sarath Menon, Matteo Rinaldi, Thomas Hammerschmidt, Matous Mrovec, Aidan Thompson, Gábor Csányi, Christoph Ortner, Ralf Drautz
models.paperTitle: Performant implementation of the atomic cluster expansion (PACE) and application to copper and silicon

models.name: PFP
models.oneLiner: First commercial universal NNP covering 45 (later 72+) elements; powers Matlantis
models.description: PFP from Preferred Networks/ENEOS was the first genuinely universal neural network potential trained to cover arbitrary combinations of 45 elements (later extended to 72+), built on the TeaNet architecture and a large curated dataset of virtual structures. It predates and arguably anticipates the MACE-MP-0/CHGNet foundation-model wave, and is commercially deployed as the engine behind the Matlantis simulation platform. It is the key closed-source counterpoint in any MLIP family tree.
models.authors: So Takamoto, Chikashi Shinagawa, Daisuke Motoki, Kosuke Nakago, Wenwen Li, Iori Kurata, Takeshi Ibuka, et al.
models.paperTitle: Towards universal neural network potential for material discovery applicable to arbitrary combination of 45 elements

models.name: PaiNN
models.oneLiner: Cheap rotationally-equivariant vector features; predicts tensorial properties and spectra
models.description: Achieves equivariance without expensive higher-order tensor products by carrying both scalar and Cartesian *vector* (l=1) features per atom and mixing them with simple, cheap equivariant operations. This gets DimeNet-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost, while unlocking targets invariant models structurally cannot express: dipole moments, polarizabilities, and IR/Raman spectra. It remains one of the best accuracy-per-FLOP QM9 models and a workhorse inside SchNetPack.
models.authors: Kristof T. Schütt, Oliver T. Unke, Michael Gastegger
models.paperTitle: Equivariant message passing for the prediction of tensorial properties and molecular spectra

models.name: SphereNet
models.oneLiner: Spherical message passing: complete 3D structure identification via (d, θ, φ) spherical coordinates
models.description: Liu et al. reframed 3D molecular representation in the spherical coordinate system, showing that distance, angle and torsion (d, θ, φ) relative to a local reference suffice to identify a 3D graph completely. Their spherical message passing (SMP) scheme captures this efficiently, and SphereNet implements it with a spherical basis. The contribution is as much theoretical as architectural — a clean completeness argument for what geometric information an invariant net must carry — and it ships as part of the DIG library.
models.authors: Yi Liu, Limei Wang, Meng Liu, Yuchao Lin, Xuan Zhang, Bora Oztekin, Shuiwang Ji
models.paperTitle: Spherical Message Passing for 3D Molecular Graphs

models.name: SpookyNet
models.oneLiner: Force field with explicit charge/spin embeddings and nonlocal attention interactions
models.description: Unke et al. attacked two assumptions baked into most ML force fields: that electronic state can be ignored, and that chemistry is strictly local. SpookyNet takes total charge and spin as explicit inputs via electronic embeddings, and adds a nonlocal interaction block based on self-attention alongside local ones, plus physically motivated electrostatics and dispersion. The effect is dramatic where it matters — on unknown spin states a baseline without electronic embeddings gave 444.6 meV MAE versus 68.0 meV with them. It can distinguish charge/spin isomers that are geometrically identical, which purely geometric nets provably cannot.
models.authors: Oliver T. Unke, Stefan Chmiela, Michael Gastegger, Kristof T. Schütt, Huziel E. Sauceda, Klaus-Robert Müller
models.paperTitle: SpookyNet: Learning force fields with electronic degrees of freedom and nonlocal effects

keyMetrics.metric: MAE with vs without electronic embeddings

models.name: ALIGNN-FF
models.fullName: Atomistic Line Graph Neural Network Force Field
models.oneLiner: Line-graph universal force field for 89 elements, trained on JARVIS-DFT
models.description: ALIGNN-FF extends the ALIGNN property-prediction architecture — which uses a line graph over bonds to encode bond angles explicitly — into a force field with energy, force and stress heads. Trained on the JARVIS-DFT dataset (~75k materials, millions of energy-force entries), it was one of the earliest 'unified force field for the periodic table' claims, contemporaneous with M3GNet. It supports fast structure relaxation and was coupled to genetic-algorithm crystal-structure prediction for alloys. It is now historically important rather than competitive: on Matbench Discovery the MPtrj-retrained ALIGNN-FF entry does not post a competitive F1.
models.authors: Kamal Choudhary, Brian DeCost, Lily Major, Keith Butler, Jeyan Thiyagalingam, Francesca Tavazza
models.paperTitle: Unified Graph Neural Network Force-field for the Periodic Table

keyMetrics.value: JARVIS-DFT (~75k materials); Matbench Discovery entry retrained on MPtrj
not reported (entry present, no compliant F1)

models.name: Allegro
models.oneLiner: Strictly local equivariant potential with no message passing, scaling to 100M atoms
models.description: Allegro is a strictly local equivariant deep learning interatomic potential that achieves both high accuracy and excellent parallel scalability. It learns many-body functions of atomic coordinates through a series of tensor products of learned equivariant representations, but without relying on message passing — removing the communication bottleneck that limits MPNN parallelism. It improves on state-of-the-art on QM9 and revised MD-17, with a single tensor product layer outperforming deep message passing networks and transformers on QM9, and shows remarkable out-of-distribution generalization. The authors demonstrated parallel scaling with a 100 million atom dynamics simulation.
models.authors: Albert Musaelian, Simon Batzner, Anders Johansson, Lixin Sun, Cameron J. Owen, Mordechai Kornbluth, Boris Kozinsky
institutions: Robert Bosch Research and Technology Center
models.paperTitle: Learning local equivariant representations for large-scale atomistic dynamics

models.name: BOTNet
models.oneLiner: Simplified, interpretable NequIP ablation that mapped the equivariant design space
models.description: BOTNet accompanies a systematic theoretical framework unifying E(3)-equivariant atom-centered interatomic potentials into a single design space. BOTNet itself is a much-simplified, interpretable version of NequIP that maintains accuracy on benchmark datasets. The paper's value is diagnostic: it performs an ablation study of NequIP examining in-domain and out-of-domain accuracy plus smooth extrapolation far from training data, isolating which architectural choices actually matter. This analysis directly motivated MACE, from largely the same group.
models.authors: Ilyes Batatia, Simon Batzner, Dávid Péter Kovács, Albert Musaelian, Gregor N. C. Simm, Ralf Drautz, Christoph Ortner, Boris Kozinsky, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: The design space of E(3)-equivariant atom-centred interatomic potentials

models.name: ComENet
models.fullName: Complete and Efficient Message Passing Network
models.oneLiner: Complete 3D information within a 1-hop neighborhood — orders of magnitude faster than DimeNet/GemNet
models.description: Wang, Liu, Lin, Liu and Ji formalized what completeness means for 3D message passing and showed that prior schemes buy it with expensive multi-hop (triplet/quadruplet) computation whose cost blows up with neighborhood size. ComENet achieves both global and local completeness using only 1-hop neighborhoods by fixing a per-atom local frame from a rotation-determining reference neighbor, yielding orders-of-magnitude speedups at competitive accuracy. It represents the efficiency endpoint of the invariant angular line before equivariant architectures took over the leaderboards.
models.authors: Limei Wang, Yi Liu, Yuchao Lin, Haoran Liu, Shuiwang Ji
models.paperTitle: ComENet: Towards Complete and Efficient Message Passing for 3D Molecular Graphs

keyMetrics.value: orders of magnitude faster than prior complete methods

models.name: DPA-1
models.oneLiner: DeepPot-SE plus gated self-attention and type embeddings — the first pretrained Deep Potential
models.description: Adds a gated attention mechanism over neighbor features to the DeepPot-SE descriptor and replaces per-element networks with a shared network plus learned type embeddings, so a single model can span many elements. Pretrained on large-scale datasets covering 56 elements, DPA-1 fine-tunes to downstream tasks with far better sample efficiency than training from scratch and generalizes to unseen elements. A striking interpretability result: the learned type-embedding vectors arrange themselves into a spiral in latent space that mirrors the periodic table. This is the pivot point where the Deep Potential line turns into the large-atomic-model / foundation-model program.
models.authors: Duo Zhang, Hangrui Bi, Fu-Zhi Dai, Wanrun Jiang, Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang
institutions: Institute of Applied Physics and Computational Mathematics, Beijing
models.paperTitle: Pretraining of attention-based deep learning potential model for molecular simulation

keyMetrics.value: improved vs DeepPot-SE; generalizes to unseen elements

models.name: DeepH
models.oneLiner: Learns the DFT Hamiltonian matrix itself rather than energies, giving full electronic structure
models.description: DeepH predicts the ab initio DFT Hamiltonian matrix in a localized basis directly from structure, then diagonalizes it to recover the full electronic structure at a fraction of DFT cost. This is a categorically different target from energy/force MLIPs: it yields band structures, wavefunctions, and transport properties. It founded the ML-Hamiltonian branch and supports ABACUS, OpenMX, FHI-aims, and SIESTA.
models.authors: He Li, Zun Wang, Nianlong Zou, Meng Ye, Runzhang Xu, Xiaoxun Gong, Wenhui Duan, Yong Xu
institutions: Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences
models.paperTitle: Deep-learning density functional theory Hamiltonian for efficient ab initio electronic-structure calculation

keyMetrics.value: full DFT Hamiltonian matrix, not just energy/forces

models.name: Equiformer
models.oneLiner: Transformer built from irreps features and equivariant graph attention on 3D atomistic graphs
models.description: Equiformer takes the standard Transformer block and replaces every operation with an SE(3)/E(3)-equivariant counterpart over irreducible-representation (irreps) features, adding tensor products and depthwise tensor-product message passing. Its key novelty is equivariant graph attention using MLP attention plus non-linear messages, which outperforms plain dot-product attention on irreps. It became the canonical demonstration that attention, not just convolution, works for equivariant atomistic modeling.
models.authors: Yi-Lun Liao, Tess Smidt
models.paperTitle: Equiformer: Equivariant Graph Attention Transformer for 3D Atomistic Graphs

models.name: GemNet-OC
models.oneLiner: GemNet redesigned on OC20-scale data, with an interaction hierarchy and 10x cheaper training
models.description: Gasteiger et al. systematically ablated architecture and hyperparameters across dataset scales and found that conclusions drawn on small molecular benchmarks do not transfer to large, diverse catalysis data — a methodological warning to the whole field. GemNet-OC introduces an interaction hierarchy separating cheap long-range from expensive short-range quadruplet/dihedral terms, making four-body interactions tractable on big adsorbate-slab systems. It trains 10x cheaper than its predecessor while outperforming prior state of the art by 16% on OC20, and advocates moderately sized proxy sets like OC-2M for fast development cycles.
models.authors: Johannes Gasteiger, Muhammed Shuaibi, Anuroop Sriram, Stephan Günnemann, Zachary Ulissi, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Abhishek Das
models.paperTitle: GemNet-OC: Developing Graph Neural Networks for Large and Diverse Molecular Simulation Datasets

models.name: Graphormer-3D
models.oneLiner: Graphormer adapted to 3D coordinates; won the Open Catalyst Challenge at NeurIPS 2021
models.description: Extends Graphormer from 2D topology to 3D atomistic systems by replacing shortest-path attention bias with continuous Gaussian-basis distance encodings, plus architectural refinements for large-scale training. It dominated the NeurIPS 2021 Open Catalyst Challenge and cut error substantially on PCQM4M. Its central claim is that a global receptive field beats local message passing — a thesis EScAIP and later scalable-attention MLIPs would revive.
models.authors: Yu Shi, Shuxin Zheng, Guolin Ke, Yifei Shen, Jiacheng You, Jiyan He, Shengjie Luo, Chang Liu, Di He, Tie-Yan Liu
models.paperTitle: Benchmarking Graphormer on Large-Scale Molecular Modeling Datasets

models.name: M3GNet
models.oneLiner: First truly universal GNN interatomic potential covering 89 elements of the periodic table
models.description: M3GNet extended the MEGNet graph-network family with explicit three-body angular interactions and a full many-body potential-energy-surface head (energy, forces, stress), trained on ~188k Materials Project relaxation trajectories (MPF.2021.2.8). It was the first model marketed as a 'universal' interatomic potential spanning 89 elements, usable as a DFT-surrogate crystal relaxer without system-specific retraining. The authors screened 31 million hypothetical crystals and identified ~1.8 million potentially stable candidates, demonstrating that a single MLIP could drive large-scale materials discovery. Though now far down the Matbench Discovery leaderboard (F1 0.569), it defined the template that CHGNet, MACE-MP and every later universal MLIP followed.
models.authors: Chi Chen, Shyue Ping Ong
models.paperTitle: A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table

models.name: MACE
models.fullName: Multi-ACE / Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing
models.oneLiner: ACE many-body expansion inside an equivariant MPNN; 2 layers, 4-body messages
models.description: Diagnoses that conventional equivariant MPNNs are slow because two-body messages force expressivity to come from stacking many layers, then fixes it by using the ACE product basis to form higher body-order messages within each layer. With four-body messages, just two message-passing iterations suffice, giving a fast, parallelizable model at state-of-the-art accuracy on rMD17, 3BPA, and AcAc. MACE is the pivotal synthesis of the density/ACE branch with the GNN branch, and became the architecture underlying a generation of foundation models.
models.authors: Ilyes Batatia, Dávid Péter Kovács, Gregor N. C. Simm, Christoph Ortner, Gábor Csányi
models.paperTitle: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields

models.name: OpenFF BespokeFit
models.oneLiner: Automated per-molecule bespoke torsion parameter generation at scale
models.description: BespokeFit accepts that no transferable parameter set is optimal for every molecule, and instead automates generating molecule-specific (bespoke) SMIRNOFF torsion parameters on demand: it fragments the molecule, runs QM torsion drives on the fragments, and fits dedicated torsion terms, all as an orchestrated workflow. This trades compute for accuracy on the specific ligand series you care about, and is the pragmatic classical counterpoint to the ML-generalization approach of Espaloma - rather than learning a better general typing function, it just refits locally, per molecule.
models.authors: Joshua T. Horton, Simon Boothroyd, Jeffrey Wagner, Joshua A. Mitchell, Trevor Gokey, David L. Dotson, Pavan Kumar Behara, Venkata Krishnan Ramaswamy, Mark Mackey, John D. Chodera, Jamshed Anwar, David L. Mobley, Daniel J. Cole
models.paperTitle: Open Force Field BespokeFit: Automating Bespoke Torsion Parametrization at Scale

keyMetrics.value: per-molecule QM torsion drives on fragments

models.name: OpenMM-ML
models.oneLiner: High-level API for running pretrained MLIPs and ML/MM hybrid systems inside OpenMM
models.description: OpenMM-ML is the deployment bridge that made pretrained molecular MLIPs usable for real biomolecular simulation rather than benchmark tables. It provides a high-level API to set up OpenMM MD with pretrained ML models in a few lines, either replacing all interactions or — critically — mixing an ML potential for a region of interest (e.g. a ligand) with a conventional force field for the rest, the ML/MM hybrid pattern that dominates practical drug-discovery use. It supports an unusually broad model zoo: MACE variants (MACE-OFF23, MACE-MPA-0, MACE-OMAT-0, MACE-OMOL-0), AIMNet2, TorchMD-Net and AceFF, FeNNol/FeNNix-Bio1, Orb models, NequIP and Allegro, ANI-1ccx and ANI-2x via TorchANI, DeePMD-kit, and any model exposing an ASE Calculator interface.
models.authors: Peter Eastman, John D. Chodera, and the OpenMM developers
models.paperTitle: OpenMM-ML: machine learning potentials in OpenMM (software)

keyMetrics.value: MACE (OFF23/MPA-0/OMAT-0/OMOL-0), AIMNet2, TorchMD-Net/AceFF, FeNNol, Orb, NequIP, Allegro, ANI-1ccx/2x, DeePMD-kit, any ASE Calculator
pure ML or ML/MM mixed systems

models.name: TorchMD-NET (ET)
models.oneLiner: Equivariant transformer with modified attention; best QM9 HOMO among classic architectures
models.description: Brings the transformer's attention mechanism into the equivariant setting, using a modified multi-head attention with distance-dependent edge weighting over vector and scalar features. Notably strong on electronic targets — its 20.3 meV HOMO leads the classic architecture family — while remaining competitive on energies, and it serves double duty as an MLIP on MD17 and ANI-1. Ablations in the paper quantified how much equivariance actually buys (removing it degraded U0 by ~6% but aspirin forces by ~174%). The TorchMD-NET codebase is now widely used infrastructure.
models.authors: Philipp Thölke, Gianni De Fabritiis
models.paperTitle: TorchMD-NET: Equivariant Transformers for Neural Network based Molecular Potentials

models.name: Transformer-M
models.oneLiner: One transformer with separate 2D and 3D channels, trained jointly on both modalities
models.description: Most models commit to either a 2D topological graph or a 3D conformer. Transformer-M adds two parallel encoding channels to a Graphormer backbone — one for 2D shortest-path structure, one for 3D distances — activating whichever the input provides, so a single set of weights trains on both 2D and 3D data and transfers between them. This lets abundant 2D data regularize 3D prediction, giving strong PCQM4Mv2 and QM9 results and a genuinely general-purpose molecular encoder. A key conceptual step toward multimodal molecular foundation models.
models.authors: Shengjie Luo, Tianlang Chen, Yixian Xu, Shuxin Zheng, Tie-Yan Liu, Liwei Wang, Di He
models.paperTitle: One Transformer Can Understand Both 2D & 3D Molecular Data

keyMetrics.value: 17.5 meV — best on the paper's QM9 table

models.name: Uni-Mol / Uni-Mol+
models.oneLiner: 3D-native pretrained molecular transformer; Uni-Mol+ iteratively refines conformers to equilibrium
models.description: Uni-Mol pretrains an SE(3)-aware transformer directly on 3D conformations (209M molecular conformations plus 3M protein pockets) with 3D position-denoising objectives, rather than on 2D graphs or SMILES — making 3D structure the primary modality and giving strong MoleculeNet and docking/binding results. Uni-Mol+ addresses the deployment gap that DFT equilibrium geometries are unavailable at inference: a two-track transformer starts from a cheap RDKit conformer and *iteratively refines it toward the DFT equilibrium* while predicting the property, setting the PCQM4Mv2 record.
models.authors: Gengmo Zhou, Zhifeng Gao, Guolin Ke et al. (Uni-Mol); Shuqi Lu, Zhifeng Gao, Di He, Linfeng Zhang, Guolin Ke (Uni-Mol+)
models.paperTitle: Uni-Mol: A Universal 3D Molecular Representation Learning Framework; Highly Accurate Quantum Chemical Property Prediction with Uni-Mol+

models.name: ViSNet
models.oneLiner: Equivariant GNN using runtime geometry calculation over vector-scalar interactions instead of spherical harmonics.
models.description: ViSNet keeps only scalar and Cartesian vector features per node and introduces a runtime geometry calculation (RGC) strategy that implicitly recovers angles, dihedrals and improper torsions from inner and outer products of direction vectors, at linear time complexity. Vector-scalar interactive message passing then mixes these channels without any Clebsch-Gordan machinery. It hits strong accuracy on MD17, rMD17, MD22, QM9 and Molecule3D at low cost, and underpins Microsoft's AI2BMD ab initio biomolecular dynamics work; a ViSNet variant took 2nd place in OGB-LSC PCQM4Mv2.
models.authors: Yusong Wang, Tong Wang, Shaoning Li, Xinheng He, Mingyu Li, Zun Wang, Nanning Zheng, Bin Shao, Tie-Yan Liu
models.paperTitle: Enhancing geometric representations for molecules with equivariant vector-scalar interactive message passing

models.name: e3nn
models.oneLiner: Modular PyTorch framework for building any E(3)-equivariant network
models.description: e3nn is a generalized framework for creating E(3)-equivariant trainable functions, operating natively on geometry and geometric tensors that transform predictably under change of coordinate system. Its core is equivariant primitives such as the TensorProduct class and spherical harmonics, composable into convolutions and attention. Critically, these primitives can express Tensor Field Networks, 3D Steerable CNNs, Clebsch-Gordan Networks, and SE(3)-Transformers as special cases. It is infrastructure rather than a model, but it is arguably the single highest-leverage artifact in this branch: NequIP, MACE, Allegro, and many others are built on it.

models.description: Yu, Qu, Houston, Conte, Nandi and Bowman pushed the many-body water expansion to an explicit four-body term, all at CCSD(T), fitted with PIPs to tens of thousands of ab initio 2-, 3- and 4-body energies for an arbitrary number of monomers. It was the first strictly first-principles many-body water potential with no lower-level or induction stand-in through 4-body, and it was benchmarked on water hexamer isomers via harmonic frequencies and diffusion Monte Carlo zero-point energies. Together with MB-pol it defines the current 'gold standard' tier for water, and the two are the standard pair in status-report comparisons of machine-learned water potentials.

models.name: sGDML for large molecules (MD22)
models.fullName: Global sGDML force fields for molecules with hundreds of atoms
models.oneLiner: Iterative solver scaling global sGDML to several hundred atoms; introduces MD22
models.description: Chmiela and co-workers removed the size ceiling on global gradient-domain models with an exact, parameter-free iterative training scheme, scaling sGDML to systems of several hundred atoms without truncating interactions or imposing any locality cutoff. models.name: GNoME
models.oneLiner: DeepMind's active-learning discovery pipeline that claimed 2.2M new crystals and 380k stable ones
models.description: GNoME is less a single potential than an active-learning flywheel: graph networks predict stability over candidate compositions generated by substitution and random structure search, DFT verifies the winners, and the verified data is fed back to retrain. Scaled across many rounds it reported 2.2 million new crystal structures with ~380,000 predicted stable, expanding the known stable-inorganic-materials set by roughly an order of magnitude, and its data was used to train a NequIP-based universal potential capable of zero-shot MD. It posts a strong F1 of 0.829 on Matbench Discovery but is flagged non-compliant/proprietary because the GNoME training set is not openly released. It is the canonical demonstration that dataset scale, not architecture, was the binding constraint on universal MLIPs.

models.name: GRACE
models.oneLiner: ACE generalized with graph basis functions; foundation models on a new accuracy-efficiency Pareto front
models.description: GRACE extends the atomic cluster expansion — a systematically complete polynomial basis for many-body interactions — with graph basis functions, giving a semilocal description that captures what equivariant message passing does but in a physically and chemically transparent, explicitly complete form. The framework is layer-parameterized (GRACE-1L/2L/3L) trading locality for accuracy. The 2025 foundation-model paper trains GRACE on the largest available materials corpora (MPtrj, OMat24, sAlex) and establishes a new Pareto front for accuracy versus inference cost: GRACE-3L-OAM-L reaches F1 0.925 with an excellent kappa-SRME of 0.121 at only 42.1M parameters, making it among the best models available for phonons and thermal conductivity.

models.name: MACE-MP-0
models.fullName: MACE Materials Project foundation model, generation 0
models.oneLiner: The model that popularized the word 'foundation model' in atomistic materials chemistry
models.description: MACE-MP-0 applied the MACE higher-order equivariant message-passing architecture to the full MPtrj dataset, releasing small/medium/large variants distinguished by maximum message equivariance (L=0,1,2). Its landmark claim was not leaderboard accuracy but out-of-the-box robustness: stable MD across molecules, solids, surfaces, liquids and interfaces it never saw in training, at PBE(+U) quality, with essentially zero user effort. This 'download it and run MD on anything' framing, plus a permissive MIT license and ASE/LAMMPS integration, made it the most widely adopted universal MLIP and effectively democratized the field. Successive revisions MACE-MP-0b, 0b2 and 0b3 fixed pathologies rather than changing data — notably isolated-atom/dimer behaviour, high-pressure stability and spurious low-density minima — with 0b3 the recommended MPtrj-only checkpoint.

It targets the accuracy and transferability gap left by 50 years of classical empirical force fields in drug discovery, crystal structure prediction, and biomolecular dynamics. It produces accurate dihedral torsion scans of unseen molecules, reliable molecular crystals and liquids including quantum nuclear effects, free energy surfaces in explicit solvent, peptide folding dynamics, and can simulate a fully solvated small protein with accurate secondary structure and vibrational spectrum.

models.description: MLIP-3 rebuilds the MTP package around active learning at the level of individual atomic neighborhoods instead of whole configurations. This matters for large simulations, where only a handful of atoms in a big cell are extrapolative — the code can then carve out and recompute small clusters rather than the entire system. It also improves the training algorithms and code structure over MLIP-2. It is the currently maintained reference implementation of moment tensor potentials.

models.oneLiner: Generative (not a potential): diffusion over lattice, coordinates and elements, steerable by property
models.description: Included as a contrast: MatterGen is generative, not an interatomic potential. It is a diffusion model that jointly denoises atomic fractional coordinates, element identities and lattice vectors, trained on 600k+ known materials and fine-tunable to steer generation toward chemistry, symmetry, or mechanical/electronic/magnetic property targets. Its structures are >2x more likely to be new and stable and >10x closer to a local energy minimum than prior generative models. It pairs naturally with MLIPs, which screen and relax what it proposes.

models.oneLiner: Unconstrained transformer on point clouds + post-hoc exact rotational symmetrization
models.description: PET is a deliberately unconstrained transformer over atom-centered edge vectors: exactly invariant to translations and permutations, but NOT rotationally equivariant by construction — it learns rotational symmetry from data. The paper's second contribution is a symmetrization protocol that makes any such model exactly equivariant post hoc, with near-zero accuracy cost. PET is the flagship argument that hard-coded equivariance is a convenience, not a necessity, and its accuracy on molecular and solid datasets made that argument stick.

models.description: QHNet predicts quantum Hamiltonian matrices for molecules using an equivariant architecture that unifies the construction of diagonal and off-diagonal matrix blocks, sharply reducing the number of tensor-product pathways versus earlier designs. Released as part of the AIRS/OpenDFT suite, it is a key efficiency milestone for the ML-Hamiltonian branch on molecular systems.
models.authors: Haiyang Yu, Zhao Xu, Xiaofeng Qian, Xiaoning Qian, Shuiwang Ji

models.name: SO3krates
models.oneLiner: Euclidean transformer separating invariant/equivariant info to avoid tensor products
models.description: SO3krates is a transformer architecture combining sparse equivariant representations (Euclidean variables) with a self-attention mechanism that separates invariant and equivariant information, eliminating the need for expensive tensor products. This yields a distinctive combination of accuracy, stability, and speed, directly targeting the well-documented instability of machine-learned force fields over extended MD timescales. It enabled simulations spanning peptides to supramolecular nanostructures, and is the semi-local backbone later reused in SO3LR.

models.name: TensorNet
models.fullName: TensorNet: Cartesian Tensor Representations for Efficient Learning of Molecular Potentials
models.oneLiner: O(3)-equivariant MPNN whose features are rank-2 Cartesian tensors mixed by plain matrix products.
models.description: TensorNet embeds each atom as a rank-2 Cartesian tensor built from direction vectors, so equivariant feature mixing reduces to ordinary matrix multiplication rather than Clebsch-Gordan tensor products. The rank-2 tensor decomposes cheaply into its scalar (trace), antisymmetric (vector) and symmetric-traceless parts, which correspond to l=0,1,2 irreps and can be processed separately. It matches or beats higher-rank spherical models on rMD17 and QM9 with far fewer parameters and much lower cost, and it is the architecture that made 'Cartesian instead of spherical' credible for mainstream molecular MLIPs. It generates a cheap RDKit conformer and iteratively optimizes it toward the equilibrium structure inside the network, predicting the property from the refined geometry. models.name: Wigner Kernels
models.fullName: Wigner kernels: body-ordered equivariant machine learning without a basis
models.oneLiner: Fully equivariant body-ordered kernels computed iteratively, independent of basis size
models.description: Sidesteps the discrete radial-chemical basis entirely by computing equivariant, body-ordered kernels directly via iterative Wigner-matrix contractions. Cost is independent of the radial-chemical basis size and grows only linearly with maximum body order, escaping the exponential scaling that limits explicit feature-based high-body-order models. It is a conceptually clean answer to the density branch's central scaling problem and a reminder that kernel methods remain theoretically competitive. Preprint 2023; published JCP 2024.

models.name: eSCN
models.oneLiner: Reduces SO(3) tensor products to SO(2), cutting cost from O(L^6) to O(L^3)
models.description: eSCN solves the central scaling bottleneck of equivariant networks: tensor products grow steeply in cost with representation degree L. By rotating node embeddings so their primary axis aligns with the edge vector, the paper shows SO(3) convolutions reduce to mathematically equivalent SO(2) convolutions, sparsifying the tensor product and reducing complexity from O(L^6) to O(L^3). This unlocked practical use of high-degree representations and achieved state-of-the-art on the large-scale OC-20 and OC-22 datasets. It is a key enabling primitive adopted by EquiformerV2 and eSEN.
