models.oneLiner: ACE reformulated entirely with Cartesian coordinates — complete, CG-free, with learned element embeddings.
models.description: Cheng rebuilt the atomic cluster expansion in Cartesian coordinates, showing that a complete description of atomic environments with controlled body order can be obtained without spherical harmonics or Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. CACE combines this Cartesian ACE basis with low-dimensional learned embeddings of chemical elements and inter-atomic message passing, giving a compact, transferable and fast potential. It is a direct conceptual bridge from MTP's moment tensors to the modern ACE/MACE family, and the codebase also supports long-range/charge-aware extensions (cace-lr).
models.authors: Bingqing Cheng
institutions: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
models.paperTitle: Cartesian atomic cluster expansion for machine learning interatomic potentials

models.name: CIDER
models.oneLiner: Nonlocal machine-learned exchange functional transferable across molecules and solids
models.description: CIDER is a machine-learned nonlocal exchange functional using compressed density descriptors that is transferable across both molecules and solids, a scope where DM21 and most ML functionals are molecule-focused. The CIDER24X variant is additionally trained on band gaps. Distributed as CiderPress with GPAW and PySCF interfaces, it is the leading solid-state-capable ML functional.
models.authors: Kyle Bystrom, Stefano Falletta, Boris Kozinsky
models.paperTitle: Nonlocal machine-learned exchange functional for molecules and solids

keyMetrics.value: Training Machine-Learned Density Functionals on Band Gaps, JCTC 20(17), 7516 (2024), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c00999

models.name: ChargE3Net
models.oneLiner: Higher-order equivariant network for charge density prediction in materials
models.description: ChargE3Net predicts electronic charge density in materials using higher-order (l > 1) equivariant representations on probe points, showing that increasing tensor order materially improves density prediction where earlier invariant models like DeepDFT plateaued. Trained across Materials Project, QM9, and NMC datasets, it is the strongest modern demonstration of the equivariance-order effect in the density-prediction branch.
models.authors: Teddy Koker, Keegan Quigley, Eric Taw, Kevin Tibbetts, Lin Li
models.paperTitle: Higher-order equivariant neural networks for charge density prediction in materials

keyMetrics.value: higher-order equivariant features improve charge density accuracy

models.name: EScAIP
models.oneLiner: Neighbor-level multi-head attention + optimized GPU kernels; 10x faster inference than prior NNIPs
models.description: EScAIP argues that NNIP progress should come from scaling a simple, hardware-efficient architecture rather than from ever-more-elaborate physics constraints. It applies multi-head self-attention at neighbor-level representations inside a GNN, implemented with highly optimized attention kernels, yielding at least 10x faster inference and 5x lower memory than existing NNIPs while topping OC20, materials and molecular benchmarks. It was also the first purely academic/national-lab model to top the leaderboard rather than a big-tech team.
models.authors: Eric Qu, Aditi S. Krishnapriyan
models.paperTitle: The Importance of Being Scalable: Improving the Speed and Accuracy of Neural Network Interatomic Potentials Across Chemical Domains

models.name: Euclidean Fast Attention (EFA)
models.oneLiner: Linear-scaling attention for Euclidean data with rotary positional encodings (ERoPE)
models.description: EFA is a linear-scaling attention-like mechanism designed for Euclidean data, addressing the quadratic cost that blocks global (long-range) atomic representations. Its key device is novel Euclidean rotary positional encodings (ERoPE) that encode spatial information while respecting physical symmetries. Applied to machine learning force fields, it lets a model capture global interactions at linear cost — the natural successor line to SO3krates from the same group, targeting long-range effects that strictly local potentials structurally cannot represent.
models.authors: J. Thorben Frank, Stefan Chmiela, Klaus-Robert Müller, Oliver T. Unke
models.paperTitle: Euclidean Fast Attention: Machine Learning Global Atomic Representations at Linear Cost

models.name: FeNNol / FeNNix
models.oneLiner: JAX library for hybrid force-field-enhanced NNPs; ships the FeNNix-Bio1 biomolecular model
models.description: FeNNol is a library for building, training and running force-field-enhanced neural network potentials. It provides a flexible modular system for hybrid models, letting users combine state-of-the-art embeddings with ML-parameterized physical interaction terms without explicit programming, and leverages JAX autodiff and JIT for fast NNP evaluation. It integrates with ASE and the Tinker-HP MD engine, and hosts pretrained models including ANI-1x/ccx, ANI-2x, MACE-OFF23, and its own FeNNix-Bio1 — which simulated condensed-phase quantum dynamics of a one-million-atom biological system with 32 RPMD beads to fully include nuclear quantum effects.
models.authors: Thomas Plé, Olivier Adjoua, Louis Lagardère, Jean-Philip Piquemal
models.paperTitle: FeNNol: an Efficient and Flexible Library for Building Force-field-enhanced Neural Network Potentials

models.name: HotPP
models.oneLiner: E(n)-equivariant message passing with arbitrary-rank Cartesian tensor nodes and messages.
models.description: HotPP generalizes Cartesian message passing beyond scalars and vectors: node embeddings and messages are Cartesian tensors of arbitrary order, coupled by a small set of elementary equivariant operations (outer product, contraction) that require no Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. Because high-rank tensors are native features, the model predicts tensorial observables — dipole moments, polarizabilities, Born charges — directly with no architectural changes. Demonstrated on phonon, infrared and Raman spectra, with ASE and LAMMPS interfaces.
models.authors: Junjie Wang, Yong Wang, Haoting Zhang, Ziyang Yang, Zhixin Liang, Jiuyang Shi, Hui-Tian Wang, Dingyu Xing, Jian Sun
models.paperTitle: E(n)-Equivariant cartesian tensor message passing interatomic potential

models.name: ICT-MPNN
models.fullName: Higher-Rank Irreducible Cartesian Tensors for Equivariant Message Passing
models.oneLiner: Formal irreducible Cartesian tensor products dropped into message passing, with equivariance and tracelessness proved.
models.description: Zaverkin and co-workers gave the Cartesian branch its missing theory: they define irreducible Cartesian tensor (ICT) products of arbitrary rank, integrate them into message-passing layers, and prove both equivariance and the traceless property of the resulting features. This closes the flexibility gap that earlier Cartesian models (TensorNet at rank 2, HotPP's reducible tensors) had relative to spherical e3nn-style architectures, while avoiding the numerically awkward Clebsch-Gordan coefficient tables. Empirically on par with or better than state-of-the-art spherical and Cartesian models; it is the theoretical parent of the TACE line.
models.authors: Viktor Zaverkin, Francesco Alesiani, Takashi Maruyama, Federico Errica, Henrik Christiansen, Makoto Takamoto, Nicolas Weber, Mathias Niepert
models.paperTitle: Higher-Rank Irreducible Cartesian Tensors for Equivariant Message Passing

models.name: Latent Ewald Summation
models.fullName: Latent Ewald summation for machine learning of long-range interactions
models.oneLiner: Learn a latent charge-like variable from local descriptors, then Ewald-sum it
models.description: Learns a latent per-atom variable from local atomic descriptors and applies a standard Ewald summation to it, recovering long-range electrostatics without ever supplying reference charges. Demonstrates that short-ranged MLIPs give unphysical predictions for charged and polar dimers, bulk water, and the water-vapour interface even when message passing is used, while the long-range model removes these artifacts at roughly twice the cost. A notably simple and general fix that has been widely adopted across architectures. Preprint 2024; published npj Comput. Mater. 2025.
models.authors: Bingqing Cheng
institutions: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
models.paperTitle: Latent Ewald summation for machine learning of long-range interactions

models.name: MACE-MPA-0
models.fullName: MACE Materials Project + Alexandria foundation model
models.oneLiner: MACE-MP retrained on MPtrj plus subsampled Alexandria — the strong MIT-licensed default
models.description: MACE-MPA-0 keeps the MACE-MP architecture but adds ~10.4M subsampled Alexandria (sAlex) structures on top of MPtrj's 1.58M, a roughly 7x data increase. The result is a large jump over MACE-MP-0 on every axis — Matbench Discovery F1 0.669 to 0.852 and kappa-SRME 0.682 to 0.412 — plus markedly better high-pressure stability and phonon accuracy, all at only 9.06M parameters. Because it stays MIT-licensed while MACE-OMAT-0 does not, MACE-MPA-0 became the practical default for most academic users and the clearest demonstration in the MACE line that data scale, not architecture, drove the 2024 accuracy jump.
models.authors: Ilyes Batatia, David P. Kovacs, Janosh Riebesell, Gabor Csanyi
models.paperTitle: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry (MACE-MPA-0 release)

models.name: MACE-OMAT-0
models.oneLiner: MACE trained on Meta's 101M-structure OMat24 corpus; excellent phonons, ASL-licensed
models.description: MACE-OMAT-0 takes the MACE foundation architecture to Meta's Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) dataset of ~101M non-equilibrium DFT structures. The heavy representation of rattled and strained configurations gives it notably strong force and phonon accuracy — both MACE-OMAT-0 and MACE-MPA-0 show much lower phonon error than MACE-MP-0b3. The catch is licensing: unlike the MIT-licensed MP/MPA checkpoints, MACE-OMAT-0 inherits the Academic Software License (ASL) from OMat24, restricting commercial use. It is the direct ancestor of MACE-MH-1, the multi-head cross-domain model trained jointly on OMAT/OMOL/OC20/MatPES at PBE, r2SCAN and wB97M-VV10 levels.
models.authors: Ilyes Batatia, David P. Kovacs, Janosh Riebesell, Gabor Csanyi
models.paperTitle: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry (MACE-OMAT-0 release)

models.name: MACE-Osaka24
models.oneLiner: First open-source NNP on a unified crystal+molecule dataset via Total Energy Alignment
models.description: MACE-Osaka24 is a multi-domain universal MLIP trained jointly on crystal and molecular datasets, and was the first open-source neural network potential built on a unified dataset spanning both domains. Its enabling contribution is Total Energy Alignment, a dataset-integration technique that reconciles first-principles calculations performed under different conditions and levels of theory into a single consistent energy scale — the central obstacle to multi-domain training, and a problem UMA later addressed differently via task-conditioned MoLE routing. It uses the MACE architecture and demonstrated that molecules and crystals need not require separate foundation models.
models.authors: Tomoya Shiota, Kenji Ishihara, Tuan Minh Do, Toshio Mori, Wataru Mizukami
institutions: Center for Quantum Information and Quantum Biology (QIQB)
models.paperTitle: Taming Multi-Domain, -Fidelity Data: Towards Foundation Models for Atomistic Scale Simulations

keyMetrics.value: Total Energy Alignment across calculation conditions
first open-source NNP on a unified molecule+crystal dataset

models.name: MOLPIPx
models.fullName: MOLPIPx: differentiable permutationally invariant polynomials in Python and Rust
models.oneLiner: End-to-end differentiable PIP library bridging PIPs to JAX-era ML frameworks
models.description: MOLPIPx makes the classical PIP basis a first-class citizen of modern autodiff tooling, exposing PIPs to linear models, neural networks and Gaussian processes through JAX and EnzymeAD-Rust backends. End-to-end differentiability means energy gradients and higher derivatives come for free, which historically was a weak point of PIP codes where gradients were numerical and slow. It is representative of where the branch is heading in 2025-2026 — alongside new PIP/fundamental-invariant generation algorithms, GPU-aided PIP-NN codes, and reverse-differentiation PIP fits for H5O2+ that deliver analytic gradients at roughly three times the cost of an energy call.
models.authors: Manuel S. Drehwald, Asma Jamali, Rodrigo A. Vargas-Hernández
models.paperTitle: MOLPIPx: An end-to-end differentiable package for permutationally invariant polynomials in Python and Rust

models.name: MatterSim
models.oneLiner: Microsoft's universal potential spanning 0-5000 K and up to 1000 GPa
models.description: MatterSim's distinguishing claim is thermodynamic coverage rather than raw leaderboard rank: it is trained on a large in-house actively-learned dataset deliberately sampled across temperatures from 0 to 5000 K and pressures up to 1000 GPa, targeting free energies and finite-temperature properties that MPtrj-trained models — which see mostly near-0 K relaxation snapshots — extrapolate badly. Released in M3G and 5M sizes, the 5M variant posts F1 0.862 on Matbench Discovery at only 4.55M parameters. The code is MIT-licensed and hosted by Microsoft, but Matbench Discovery flags it non-compliant because the MatterSim training set itself is proprietary and unreleased.
models.authors: Han Yang, Chenxi Hu, Yichi Zhou, Xixian Liu, Yu Shi, Jielan Li, Ziyang Sun, Zekun Chen, Zhaoxi Zhang, Ziheng Lu, Claudio Zeni, Tian Xie
models.paperTitle: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures

models.name: Nutmeg
models.oneLiner: TensorNet-based biomolecular potentials that inject precomputed partial charges as a charge reference
models.description: Nutmeg is the model family released alongside SPICE v2, the expanded quantum chemistry dataset with far more chemical-space sampling and non-covalent interaction data. Built on the TensorNet architecture, its key methodological contribution is injecting precomputed Gasteiger partial charges into the model to give it a reference for large-scale charge distribution — a cheap alternative to learned charge equilibration. The ablation is instructive and widely cited: models using formal charges have consistently higher error than those using partial charges, and models with no charge information at all have dramatically higher error on molecules with charged groups. Nutmeg reproduces conformational energy differences well even for highly charged or out-of-distribution-large molecules, produces stable MD trajectories, and is fast enough for routine small-molecule simulation.
models.authors: Peter Eastman, Benjamin P. Pritchard, John D. Chodera, Thomas E. Markland
models.paperTitle: Nutmeg and SPICE: Models and Data for Biomolecular Machine Learning
models.venue: arXiv June 2024; J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20, 8583

keyMetrics.value: partial charges < formal charges << no charges (error on charged groups)
TensorNet with injected Gasteiger partial charges
expanded chemical-space and non-covalent interaction sampling

models.name: Orb / Orb-v2
models.fullName: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
models.oneLiner: Non-equivariant, diffusion-pretrained universal potential; 3-6x faster than rivals
models.description: Orb from Orbital Materials deliberately drops rotational equivariance in favor of a plain, hardware-friendly graph network with denoising-diffusion pretraining, betting that data and speed beat symmetry priors. Orb-v1 (Sept 2024) topped Matbench Discovery; Orb-v2 (Oct 2024) cut error 31% versus other methods at release while running 3-6x faster than competing universal potentials, and stayed stable on out-of-distribution materials. It became the reference point for the 'do we actually need equivariance?' debate alongside PET and EScAIP.
models.authors: Mark Neumann, James Gin, Benjamin Rhodes, Steven Bennett, Zhiyi Li, Hitarth Choubisa, Arthur Hussey, Jonathan Godwin
models.paperTitle: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential

models.name: Orb-v1 (ORBFF)
models.fullName: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
models.oneLiner: Non-equivariant, diffusion-pretrained universal potential that traded symmetry for 3-6x speed
models.description: Orb-v1 was the field's most prominent argument that strict roto-equivariance is a design choice, not a requirement. It uses a plain (non-equivariant) message-passing graph network with a denoising-diffusion pretraining objective on unlabelled structures, then finetunes on energies and forces. On release it delivered a 31% error reduction over prior methods on Matbench Discovery while running 3-6x faster than comparable equivariant potentials, and remained stable on out-of-distribution systems across relaxation, Monte Carlo and MD. It launched the Orb line from Orbital Materials and forced a real debate about the accuracy cost of dropping equivariance.
models.authors: Mark Neumann, James Gin, Benjamin Rhodes, Steven Bennett, Zhiyi Li, Hitarth Choubisa, Arthur Hussey, Jonathan Godwin
models.paperTitle: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential

models.name: Orb-v2
models.oneLiner: Refined non-equivariant Orb; MPA variant hits F1 0.88 but kappa-SRME 1.73 exposes the direct-force flaw
models.description: Orb-v2 refined the Orb architecture and released MPtrj-only and MPtrj+Alexandria (MPA) checkpoints at 25.2M parameters, with the MPA variant reaching F1 0.880 — near the top of the leaderboard for discovery. But Orb-v2 became the field's canonical cautionary tale: its kappa-SRME of 1.73 is catastrophically bad, essentially no better than random, because directly predicting forces (rather than differentiating a conserved energy) yields a non-conservative field whose force constants are unreliable. This split between excellent F1 and terrible thermal conductivity, shared with eqV2, is precisely why Matbench Discovery elevated kappa-SRME to a headline metric and why Orb-v3 reintroduced a conservative option.
models.authors: Mark Neumann, Benjamin Rhodes, Jonathan Godwin, Tim Duignan
models.paperTitle: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential

models.name: SO3LR
models.oneLiner: Biomolecular foundation potential coupling SO3krates with universal pairwise long-range physics
models.description: SO3LR from the Tkatchenko group is the leading example of the physics-augmented route to biomolecular foundation potentials: it pairs the fast, stable SO3krates equivariant transformer for semi-local interactions with universal pairwise physical terms for short-range nuclear repulsion, long-range electrostatics, and MBD-derived dispersion, rather than trying to learn everything from data. It is trained on ~4 million neutral and charged molecular complexes at the PBE0+MBD level, giving it uniform coverage of covalent and noncovalent chemistry. It scales to ~200k atoms on a single GPU and has been demonstrated on all four major biomolecule classes, peptide folding, and nanosecond MD of a protein, a glycoprotein, and a lipid bilayer in explicit solvent. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, it currently offers the best accuracy/cost balance for biomolecular systems, and it is MIT-licensed with ASE and JAX-MD integration.
models.authors: Adil Kabylda, J. Thorben Frank, Sergio Suarez-Dou, Almaz Khabibrakhmanov, Leonardo Medrano Sandonas, Oliver T. Unke, Stefan Chmiela, Klaus-Robert Muller, Alexandre Tkatchenko
models.paperTitle: Molecular Simulations with a Pretrained Neural Network and Universal Pairwise Force Fields

keyMetrics.value: ~4M neutral and charged complexes at PBE0+MBD
protein, glycoprotein, lipid bilayer in explicit solvent (ns scale)

models.name: SevenNet
models.oneLiner: NequIP-based potential with an efficient multi-GPU parallelization scheme for LAMMPS MD
models.description: SevenNet is based on the NequIP architecture and contributes an efficient parallelization scheme for message-passing GNN interatomic potentials, interfacing with LAMMPS for MD. Parallelizing GNN-IPs is hard because multiple message-passing layers complicate data communication under the spatial decomposition method that MD packages prefer. On a 32-GPU cluster with SiO2, SevenNet achieves over 80% parallel efficiency in weak scaling and near-ideal strong scaling while GPUs remain fully utilized. Its pretrained SevenNet-0 (Materials Project) was used to generate amorphous Si3N4 with more than 100,000 atoms.
models.authors: Yutack Park, Jaesun Kim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han
models.paperTitle: Scalable Parallel Algorithm for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials in Molecular Dynamics Simulations

models.name: SevenNet-0
models.oneLiner: NequIP-based universal potential engineered for multi-GPU parallel LAMMPS MD
models.description: SevenNet's core contribution is systems engineering rather than a new functional form: it reworks NequIP-style multi-layer message passing so that spatial decomposition across GPUs actually works, solving the communication blow-up that multiple message-passing layers cause. Interfaced to LAMMPS, it hits >80% parallel efficiency in weak scaling on a 32-GPU cluster with near-ideal strong scaling. SevenNet-0 is the general-purpose checkpoint trained on MPtrj (an MPF-trained variant also exists), and at only 842k parameters it reaches F1 0.724 — making it the go-to universal MLIP for people who need genuinely large-scale MD rather than single-cell relaxations.
models.authors: Yutack Park, Jaesun Kim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han
models.paperTitle: Scalable Parallel Algorithm for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials in Molecular Dynamics Simulations

models.name: SevenNet-l3i5
models.fullName: SevenNet with l=3 spherical harmonics, i=5 interaction
models.oneLiner: Higher-angular-resolution SevenNet: l=3 harmonics and linear self-connection, 1.17M params
models.description: SevenNet-l3i5 raises SevenNet-0's maximum spherical-harmonic degree from l=2 to l=3, capturing higher-order angular structure, and replaces the element-dependent self-connection layer with a plain linear (self-interaction) layer, stripping out a large number of element-specific parameters. The combination buys a substantial accuracy gain — F1 0.724 to 0.760, kappa-SRME 0.762 to 0.550 — for only a modest parameter increase to 1.17M, still trained purely on MPtrj. It is a clean, well-controlled ablation of what angular resolution is worth in a universal MLIP, and remains one of the most accuracy-per-parameter efficient MPtrj-only models.
models.authors: Yutack Park, Jaesun Kim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han
models.paperTitle: Scalable Parallel Algorithm for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
models.venue: model release 2024 (J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024 architecture)

models.name: Uni-Mol2
models.fullName: Uni-Mol2: Exploring Molecular Pretraining Model at Scale
models.oneLiner: 1.1B-parameter two-track molecular transformer; first scaling law for molecular pretraining
models.description: Uni-Mol2 is the first systematic scaling-law study of molecular pretraining, fitting power-law relations between validation loss and model size, dataset size, and compute. Its two-track transformer fuses atom-level, graph-level and geometry-level features, and it scales from 84M to 1.1B parameters pretrained on 800M conformations — the largest molecular pretraining model at the time. Performance improved monotonically with scale, giving the molecular field its Kaplan-style scaling evidence.
models.authors: Xiaohong Ji, Zhen Wang, Zhifeng Gao, Hang Zheng, Linfeng Zhang, Guolin Ke, Weinan E
models.paperTitle: Uni-Mol2: Exploring Molecular Pretraining Model at Scale

models.name: eqV2 / EquiformerV2-OMat24
models.oneLiner: OMat24's 110M-structure dataset plus EquiformerV2; first to break F1 0.9 on Matbench Discovery
models.description: The OMat24 release paired a genuinely field-changing dataset — over 110 million DFT calculations deliberately sampled for structural and compositional diversity, including rattled and non-equilibrium configurations that MPtrj lacks — with EquiformerV2 checkpoints trained on it. eqV2-M was the first model to break F1 0.9 on Matbench Discovery (0.917, formation-energy accuracy ~20 meV/atom), a step change that reset expectations for the whole field. Its equally instructive failure is kappa-SRME 1.77: the direct non-conservative force head made it useless for thermal transport, a defect eSEN was built to fix. OMat24 (with MPtrj and sAlex) became the standard training recipe for nearly every top model since.
models.authors: Luis Barroso-Luque, Muhammed Shuaibi, Xiang Fu, Brandon M. Wood, Misko Dzamba, Meng Gao, Ammar Rizvi, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Zachary W. Ulissi
models.paperTitle: Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models
models.license: Open source (fairchem code MIT; OMat24 data/checkpoints under Meta ASL / CC-BY terms)

models.name: AIMNet2-NSE
models.oneLiner: Reactive open-shell NNP handling arbitrary charge and spin multiplicity via spin-charge equilibration
models.description: AIMNet2-NSE extends AIMNet2 from closed-shell to open-shell chemistry by replacing the single-channel neural charge equilibration with two-channel neural spin-charge equilibration, updating atomic alpha and beta spin-charges separately and taking total spin multiplicity S as an explicit input alongside atomic numbers, coordinates, and total charge. Its training set adds ~13 million open-shell molecules in doublet and triplet states plus 200,000 doublet radical reaction profiles to the original 14-element AIMNet2 data. It predicts radical reaction energies, barriers, and spin-crossing events at near-DFT accuracy with roughly five orders of magnitude speedup, making high-throughput radical-intermediate exploration tractable — a capability that most molecular foundation MLIPs still lack.
models.authors: Nikhil Kalita, Roman Zubatyuk, Dylan M. Anstine, Olexandr Isayev
models.paperTitle: AIMNet2-NSE: A Transferable Reactive Neural Network Potential for Open-Shell Chemistry

models.name: AlphaNet
models.oneLiner: Local-frame equivariant MLIP balancing accuracy and speed; MPtrj and OMat24 variants
models.description: AlphaNet is an equivariant GNN interatomic potential built around local-frame constructions that reduce the cost of high-degree tensor products while retaining equivariance. It ships both MPtrj-trained and OMat24-trained (OAM) checkpoints and is submitted to Matbench Discovery. It matters as one of the efficiency-oriented answers to the accuracy/throughput tradeoff that dominates the 2025 universal-potential field.
models.authors: Bangchen Yin, Jiaao Wang, Weitao Du, Yuanqi Du, Chenru Duan, Carla P. Gomes, Graeme Henkelman, Hai Xiao
models.paperTitle: AlphaNet: Scaling Up Local-frame-based Interatomic Potential

models.name: ByteFF-Pol
models.oneLiner: GNN-parameterized universal polarizable classical force field trained purely on QM data
models.description: ByteFF-Pol represents the 'GNN parameterizes a physical force field' branch rather than the 'GNN is the force field' branch: a polarizable classical force field whose parameters are predicted by a graph neural network trained on high-level QM data, with no experimental calibration. This gives classical-FF speed and transferability to bulk liquid simulation while inheriting QM accuracy, and the explicit polarization term proves decisive. It outperforms state-of-the-art classical and machine learning force fields at predicting thermodynamic and transport properties across a wide range of small-molecule liquids and electrolytes, accurately capturing density, viscosity, and conductivity of electrolyte systems simultaneously — a combination charge-fixed force fields consistently miss. Successor to ByteFF; released as ByteFF2 on GitHub and HuggingFace.
models.authors: Tianze Zheng, Zhenliang Mu, Wen Yan, Zhenyu Li, Sheng Gong, Bo Wang, Jian Jiang, ByteDance Seed team
models.paperTitle: Bridging quantum mechanics to liquid properties via a universal organic force field

keyMetrics.value: outperforms SOTA classical and ML force fields

models.name: Cartesian-nj / cartnn
models.fullName: Cartesian-nj: Extending e3nn to Irreducible Cartesian Tensor Product and Contraction
models.oneLiner: Cartesian-3j / generalized CG coefficients extending e3nn, with Cartesian MACE, NequIP and Allegro.
models.description: From the TACE group, this work defines the Cartesian-3j symbol and Cartesian generalized Clebsch-Gordan coefficients as the Cartesian-space counterpart of the spherical tensor algebra, and packages them as `cartnn`, an extension of e3nn. Using it they build Cartesian versions of MACE, NequIP and Allegro and show that irreducible Cartesian models reach accuracy comparable to their spherical variants, while being candid about the computational scaling penalty at high rank. They also train TACE-v1-OAM-M, a universal MLIP benchmarked on Matbench Discovery with performance competitive against state-of-the-art spherical-tensor uMLIPs. The v1 preprint was titled 'A Cartesian-3j Framework for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials'.
models.authors: Zemin Xu, Chenyu Wu, Wenbo Xie, P. Hu
models.paperTitle: Cartesian-nj: Extending e3nn to Irreducible Cartesian Tensor Product and Contraction — Broadening NequIP, Allegro, and MACE to Cartesian Space

models.name: DPA-3
models.oneLiner: Message-passing GNN for the LAM era with task-count-independent parameter scaling
models.description: DPA-3 replaces the hand-designed Deep Potential descriptor with a message-passing graph network built explicitly for the large-atomic-model regime. Its key architectural property is that parameter count stays constant as tasks are added under multi-task training — unlike DPA-2, where per-task heads grow the model — while still obeying PES physical constraints and exhibiting clean scaling laws. Trained as a LAM on OpenLAM-v1, DPA-3.1-3M posts the lowest overall zero-shot generalization error across 12 downstream tasks, making it a strong out-of-the-box potential needing minimal finetuning data. On Matbench Discovery, DPA3-v2-OpenLAM reaches F1 0.890; the newer DPA-4.0.1-Pro-MPtrj (arXiv:2606.02419) hits F1 0.857 with kappa-SRME 0.211 at 22.8M params trained on MPtrj alone.
models.authors: Duo Zhang, Anyang Peng, Chun Cai, Wentao Li, Yuanchang Zhou, Jinzhe Zeng, Mingyu Guo, Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang
models.paperTitle: A Graph Neural Network for the Era of Large Atomistic Models

models.name: ESNet
models.oneLiner: Transformer-architecture energy predictor for the IS2E task, trained on MP 2022
models.description: ESNet is a transformer-based model from the Institute of Computing Technology, CAS and the Ningbo Institute of AI Industry, targeting the RS2RE/IS2E energy-only prediction task rather than full force-field use. It is a Matbench Discovery entry (June 2025) that illustrates the persistent energy-only property-prediction branch running alongside full MLIPs.
models.authors: Chao Huang, Chunyan Chen, Ling Shi
institutions: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
Ningbo Institute of Artificial Intelligence Industry
models.paperTitle: ESNet (Research Square preprint)

models.name: Egret-1
models.fullName: Egret-1 / Egret-1e / Egret-1t pretrained neural network potentials
models.oneLiner: Rowan's MIT-licensed MACE-architecture NNP family for bioorganic, thermochemistry, and transition states
models.description: Egret-1 is Rowan Scientific's family of large pretrained NNPs built on the MACE architecture, targeting main-group, organic, and biomolecular chemistry. The commercial significance is licensing as much as accuracy: Egret-1 delivers MACE-OFF-class or better quality under a permissive MIT license, versus MACE-OFF's academic-only ASL. The family splits by task — Egret-1 is the general-purpose bioorganic model; Egret-1e adds main-group chemistry data and excels at thermochemistry; Egret-1t is trained on transition states and targets chemical reactivity, which is unusual for a pretrained NNP. Smaller Egret-1S and Egret-1M variants are also released. The models match or exceed routine quantum-chemical methods on torsional scans, conformer ranking, and geometry optimization with multiple-order-of-magnitude speedups.

models.name: GotenNet
models.oneLiner: E(3)-equivariant tensor network avoiding irreps and Clebsch-Gordan transforms entirely
models.description: GotenNet models the geometric intricacies of 3D graphs under strict E(3) equivariance while sidestepping the expressiveness-efficiency trade-off: it leverages effective geometric tensor representations without relying on irreducible representations or Clebsch-Gordan transforms, cutting computational overhead. It introduces a unified structural embedding, geometry-aware tensor attention, and hierarchical tensor refinement that iteratively updates edge representations via inner products on high-degree steerable features. It consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on QM9, rMD17, MD22, and Molecule3D for both scalar and high-degree property prediction.

models.name: HIENet
models.oneLiner: Interleaves cheap invariant and expensive equivariant layers to buy speed without losing high-order symmetry
models.description: HIENet confronts the central architectural trade-off in MLIPs head-on: invariant models are cheap but weak at high-order outputs, equivariant models capture high-order symmetry but cost far more. Rather than picking a side, HIENet interleaves both layer types in one network — invariant layers carry the bulk of the representation cheaply while a smaller number of equivariant layers supply the high-order angular structure — while provably satisfying key physical constraints. It reaches F1 0.777 with kappa-SRME 0.642 at 7.51M parameters on MPtrj-only training, with considerable speedups over comparable models, and generalizes the hybrid idea now appearing in several 2026 architectures.

Sage 2.3.0 is the first OpenFF force field co-fit to AshGC charges, with vdW and valence parameters re-fit and torsions split to single multiplicities. This marks the ML-parameterization approach reaching the electrostatics half of the force field, not just the valence terms. Released Jan 13, 2026.

models.name: Orb-v3
models.oneLiner: Systematically maps the accuracy-speed-memory frontier; >10x lower latency, >8x less memory than Orb-v2
models.description: Orb-v3 is the most rigorous published study of the universal-MLIP design frontier, systematically traversing the trade-offs induced by three independent knobs: roto-equivariance, conservatism (energy-differentiated vs direct forces), and graph sparsity (fixed neighbour counts). It delivers near-state-of-the-art accuracy at >10x reduced latency and >8x reduced memory versus Orb-v2, reaching F1 0.905 with kappa-SRME 0.21 at 25.5M parameters — fixing Orb-v2's thermal-conductivity collapse via conservative variants. Its headline finding, that non-equivariant and even non-conservative architectures can accurately model physical properties when trained and evaluated carefully, remains one of the field's live controversies.

models.name: OrbMol
models.oneLiner: Orb-v3 architecture trained on OMol25, accepting total charge and spin multiplicity
models.description: OrbMol extends Orbital Materials' Orb-v3 architecture — a fast, non-equivariant graph network family spanning the accuracy/speed/memory Pareto frontier — from inorganic materials to molecular systems by training on the OMol25 dataset of 100M+ high-accuracy DFT calculations. Unlike its materials-only predecessors it accepts total charge and spin multiplicity as inputs, enabling open-shell species, ionic electrolytes, metal complexes, and biomolecules. It ships in two checkpoints: OrbMol (conservative, forces as energy gradients, using the equigrad methodology to improve physical fidelity of a non-equivariant backbone) and OrbMol-direct (non-conservative direct force prediction with post-hoc mean-subtraction for zero net force and Lagrangian minimization for zero net torque). It is a leading example of a third party building a competitive molecular foundation model directly on Meta's open OMol25 data.

The result is the field's cleanest counterexample to brute-force scaling: despite a tiny training set and lightweight model, PET-MAD is competitive with state-of-the-art MLIPs on inorganic solids while remaining reliable on molecules and organic materials where MPtrj-trained models degrade. The companion PET-MAD-DOS predicts electronic density of states, Fermi levels and bandgaps from the same data. The line scales up to PET-OAM-XL (730M params, F1 0.924, kappa-SRME 0.119) in the uPET repository.

models.fullName: SevenNet Multi-Fidelity trained on OMat24 + MPtrj + sAlex
models.oneLiner: Multi-fidelity SevenNet jointly trained on OMat24, MPtrj and sAlex; F1 0.901 at 25.7M params
models.description: SevenNet-MF-ompa applies multi-fidelity learning to reconcile the three big materials corpora — OMat24, MPtrj and sAlex — which differ in DFT settings and would otherwise conflict if naively pooled. Separate fidelity heads let the model absorb OMat24's ~100M non-equilibrium structures while still calibrating to MPtrj's reference level, pushing SevenNet from F1 0.760 to 0.901 and briefly topping the Matbench Discovery leaderboard on discovery accuracy. Its weak spot is thermal transport: kappa-SRME 0.317 lags GRACE and TACE at similar F1. The line continues with SevenNet-Omni (2025, arXiv:2510.11241), trained on the COSMOS dataset, which reaches F1 0.906 with kappa-SRME 0.192 at 54.9M parameters.

models.name: Skala
models.oneLiner: Microsoft's learned XC functional reaching hybrid-level accuracy at semi-local DFT cost
models.description: Skala is not an interatomic potential but belongs on this timeline as the complementary attack on the same problem: instead of learning the PES directly, it learns the exchange-correlation functional inside DFT itself. Where traditional functional development adds increasingly expensive hand-designed features, Skala uses a scalable neural network on inexpensive input features (electron density and derived meta-GGA quantities on a 3D grid) to learn the necessary non-local representations. It surpasses state-of-the-art hybrid functionals in accuracy while retaining semi-local cost — meaning it can generate better reference data for MLIPs, and offers an orthogonal path to accuracy that MLIP foundation models inherit rather than compete with. Distributed as a PyTorch package on PyPI/conda-forge with PySCF, GPU4PySCF, and ASE bindings, and served on Azure AI Foundry.

models.name: TACE
models.fullName: Tensor Atomic Cluster Expansion (unified Irreducible Cartesian Tensor Framework)
models.oneLiner: Unified irreducible-Cartesian-tensor ACE framework doing spectral and spatial expansion with universal embeddings.
models.description: TACE is the current flagship of the Cartesian branch: it decomposes local environments into irreducible Cartesian tensors and builds a controlled many-body ACE hierarchy entirely in Cartesian space, handling arbitrary-rank reducible or irreducible tensors and extracting irreducible components of any weight. Working in Cartesian space cuts the number of arrays in a tensor product to two and eliminates Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, and TACE offers a CG-free spatial-domain alternative alongside the usual frequency-domain ACE. Universal invariant/equivariant embeddings let it absorb basis sets, charges, magnetic moments and external-field perturbations, so one framework covers energies, spectra, Hessians, field responses, charged and magnetic systems, multi-fidelity training and catalysis. Note the title has shifted across revisions (v1 'Spectral/Spatial Tensor Atomic Cluster Expansion with Universal Embeddings in Cartesian Space'); v2+ is 'TACE: A unified Irreducible Cartesian Tensor Framework for Atomistic Machine Learning'.
models.authors: Zemin Xu, Wenbo Xie, Daiqian Xie, P. Hu
models.paperTitle: TACE: A unified Irreducible Cartesian Tensor Framework for Atomistic Machine Learning

models.name: TorchSim
models.fullName: TorchSim: atomistic simulation engine in PyTorch
models.oneLiner: Torch-native batched atomistic simulation engine giving up to 100x speedup over ASE for MLIPs
models.description: TorchSim is the infrastructure layer the foundation-MLIP era needed: an open-source atomistic simulation engine written natively in PyTorch, rewriting core simulation primitives (integrators, optimizers, neighbor lists) so they run on-GPU alongside the model instead of round-tripping through ASE's Python/NumPy loop. Its decisive design choice is batching — unlike conventional MD packages that simulate one system at a time, TorchSim evolves many systems concurrently to saturate modern GPUs, enabling thousands of atoms or thousands of independent systems on a single H100. It supports MD integrators, structural relaxation, both ML and classical potentials (Lennard-Jones, Morse, soft-sphere), automatic memory management, differentiable simulation, and materials-informatics integrations, reporting up to 100x speedup over ASE with popular MLIPs.

models.name: UMA
models.oneLiner: Meta FAIR's multi-domain universal MLIP family using a mixture-of-linear-experts architecture
models.description: UMA is Meta FAIR Chemistry's family of universal atomic models trained jointly across five open-science domains — OC20 (catalysis), ODAC23 (direct air capture / MOFs), OMat24 (inorganic materials), OMol25 (molecules), and OMC25 (molecular crystals) — totaling roughly half a billion unique 3D structures, the largest MLIP training run to date. Its central novelty is the Mixture of Linear Experts (MoLE) architecture, which routes on global system metadata (charge, spin, DFT task) to merge expert linear layers into a single effective weight matrix per structure, so capacity grows without inference cost: UMA-medium carries 1.4B total parameters but only ~50M active per structure. A single generalist checkpoint matches or beats domain-specialized models on materials, molecular, and catalysis benchmarks with no fine-tuning, which is why it is the reference point for 'one model for all of chemistry' claims. Public checkpoints on HuggingFace are uma-s (1.1/1.2/1.2.1) and uma-m (1.1) under the permissive FAIR Chemistry License v1; the original uma-s-1 is archived due to a known extensivity bug.

models.name: eSEN
models.oneLiner: Meta FAIR's demonstration that PES smoothness, not just expressivity, drives physical-property accuracy
models.description: eSEN diagnosed why models like eqV2 could top discovery F1 while failing catastrophically on phonons and thermal conductivity: discontinuities and non-smoothness in the learned potential-energy surface, introduced by non-conservative force heads and hard cutoffs, wreck the second and third derivatives that phonons and kappa depend on. By enforcing smoothness and energy-conservation in an expressive equivariant architecture, eSEN-30M-OAM achieves F1 0.925 with kappa-SRME 0.17 at 30.2M parameters and runs energy-conserving MD on out-of-distribution systems. It reframed the field's evaluation criteria and directly motivated the smoothness-metric literature that followed.

models.name: eSEN-OMol25
models.fullName: equivariant Smooth Energy Network trained on Open Molecules 2025
models.oneLiner: Meta's smooth equivariant MLIP baseline for OMol25, the largest open molecular DFT dataset
models.description: OMol25 is Meta FAIR Chemistry's Open Molecules 2025 dataset: over 100 million wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD single-point calculations spanning 83 elements with explicit coverage of charges, spin states, solvation, biomolecules, electrolytes, metal complexes, and reactivity. The accompanying baseline models use the eSEN (equivariant Smooth Energy Network) architecture, which prioritizes smoothness of the potential energy surface for well-behaved MD and geometry optimization, and takes total charge and spin multiplicity as explicit inputs. eSEN-md is the strongest all-around baseline reported. OMol25 + eSEN is the direct precursor and a key training component of UMA, and the dataset has become the de facto molecular foundation-model training corpus for third parties (OrbMol, MACE-OMOL-0, and others).

models.name: AllScAIP
models.oneLiner: EScAIP + all-to-all node attention for long-range interactions; scales to ~100M training samples
models.description: AllScAIP addresses the main blind spot of cutoff-based MLIPs — long-range interactions in biomolecules and electrolytes — by adding an all-to-all node attention component to a scalable, energy-conserving attention backbone that trains on O(100M) samples. It reaches state of the art on both energy/force accuracy and physics-based evaluations on Open Molecules 2025, and runs stable long-timescale MD that recovers experimental density and heat of vaporization. It is also competitive on OMat24 materials and OC20 catalysts, making it a genuinely cross-domain recipe.

models.paperTitle: A recipe for scalable attention-based MLIPs: unlocking long-range accuracy with all-to-all node attention

models.name: CEITNet
models.oneLiner: Multi-channel Cartesian local-environment tensors with learnable channel-space many-body mixing for crystal tensors.
models.description: CEITNet targets high-order tensorial crystal properties — dielectric, piezoelectric and elastic tensors — rather than just energies and forces. It constructs a multi-channel Cartesian local-environment tensor per atom and performs many-body coupling via a learnable channel-space interaction, sidestepping the cost of spherical-harmonic equivariant models while retaining equivariance. It reports better accuracy at lower cost than spherical-harmonic baselines on standard crystal-tensor benchmarks, and is a good example of the Cartesian branch expanding from potentials into general tensorial property prediction.
models.authors: Dian Jin, Yancheng Yuan, Xiaoming Tao
models.paperTitle: Efficient Equivariant High-Order Crystal Tensor Prediction via Cartesian Local-Environment Many-Body Coupling

models.name: CliffordSTF
models.oneLiner: Couples geometric-algebra multivectors to symmetric-traceless Cartesian tracks to fix force directions.
models.description: This work diagnoses a specific failure of Cl(3,0) geometric-algebra interatomic potentials: they get force magnitudes roughly right but force directions badly wrong. CliffordSTF couples the Clifford multivector representation to closed-form symmetric-traceless Cartesian tensor tracks, restoring directional fidelity. The headline result is an order-of-magnitude relative gain in force-cosine similarity on rMD17 (0.055 to 0.551), plus 15.8% lower force MAE and 10.9% lower energy MAE, and best out-of-distribution S2EF energy MAE on OC22 among higher-order methods. It marks the convergence of geometric algebra and the Cartesian-tensor branch.
models.authors: Can Polat, Erchin Serpedin, Mustafa Kurban, Hasan Kurban
models.paperTitle: Geometric Algebra Meets Cartesian Tensors: Higher-Order Equivariance for Interatomic Potentials

models.name: EquiformerV3

models.oneLiner: Current Matbench Discovery F1 leader (0.931) at just 30.3M parameters
models.description: EquiformerV3 is the 2026 state of the art on Matbench Discovery discovery accuracy, improving the Equiformer line along three axes simultaneously: speed (a 1.75x speedup from optimized software implementation), expressivity (equivariant merged layer normalization and SwiGLU-S2 activations), and generality. Trained with a denoising auxiliary task (DeNS) on non-equilibrium structures, EquiformerV3+DeNS-OAM tops the leaderboard at F1 0.931 with a solid kappa-SRME of 0.118 at only 30.3M parameters, and posts state-of-the-art results across OC20, OMat24 and Matbench Discovery. Its MPtrj-only variant reaches F1 0.863, showing how much of the gain is data versus architecture. It represents the maturation of the equivariant-transformer branch that began with Equiformer and eqV2.
